The first half is brought to an end and tempers are flaring as the two sides head off, with the game level at 0-0 at the break. The Porto fans and players are not happy with the officiating and Enzo is also involved in some antics.

Gvardiol needs to be careful as he is not punished for delaying a restart when you consider he is already on a booking. The Porto fans want to see a second yellow but the referee says the ball was moving so Porto could not take the restart.

Three added minutes to conclude this first half.

It has been revealed that should Guehi be in trouble here? He appears in real time to win his header but when you watch the replays he led with his arm. He catches Veiga right in the face and Guehi could be in some strife. However, VAR is not going to take any further action and Guehi can count himself lucky. The medics are on to tend to Veiga and you do wonder why VAR has not recommended a review. The ridiculous thing about that was that Guehi was not punished with a yellow card or even a free-kick. That clearly indicates the referee did not properly see it.

Porto fans quick to remind Ruben Dias and Enzo Fernandez of their Benfica history. They jeered the pair when they got on the ball. Enzo is getting it from all angles at the moment, with Coventry fans taunting him at the weekend. He can expect more of that in the Premier League after his part in England’s exit at the World Cup, which led to Argentina players holding up a flag saying the Falkland Islands were Argentina’s.

In a recent development, tensions are boiling over. They have been threatening to do so between Gomes and Gvardiol for a little while and now they do. Gomes steals the ball off Gvardiol and attempts to counter but is pulled back by Gvardiol, who is rightly booked. Gomes is not happy with Gvardiol and they come to blows.

It has been revealed that D Costa twice denies Manchester City in a matter of seconds. First he saves from Haaland, then gets to his feet to deny Cherki. Manchester City are knocking on the door and you do feel like a goal is coming for Enzo Maresca’s side.

No goals in Porto but Real Madrid have their second at home against Inter Milan through Fede Valverde.

Manchester City struggled to carve out any genuine chances in the opening quarter of an hour but there are creating more and more opportunities, the latest falling to Foden, whose shot from the right side of the box looking for the far corner is saved by D Costa.

It has been revealed that it is not often you see Haaland miss two good chances with his head in quick succession but that is what has happened. Semenyo cuts inside on the left onto his right and curls in a cross into a good area. He picks out Haaland but the Norwegian’s header misses the target. He knows he should have done better as he shakes his head in frustration.

Porto’s front three have struggled to have much of an impact in the game, in particular Silva up top, who has been almost non-existent.

It has been revealed that A great save from D Costa to deny Haaland. Foden’s cross just before the byline on the left side of the box picks out Haaland. The Norwegian has barely touched the ball tonight but comes close to opening the scoring. However, D Costa is on hand to deny him with a fine save. Should Haaland have given D Costa the chance to save it? Maybe not.

Diogo Costa CLAWS away Erling Haaland's header 🧤Man City come closest so far in Porto 👀 pic.twitter.com/KVnBHdbNlH.

In probably the marquee match-up of the night, Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid are taking on Inter Milan at the Bernabeu. Real have just taken the lead through Kylian Mbappe.

Semenyo cuts inside from the left and gets a shot away from the edge of the box but it is straight at D Costa. That was Manchester City’s first shot of the night.

In a recent development, veiga has a shot saved at the near post by Donnarumma but the offside flag goes up. Veiga and Pep exchange a neat one-two down Porto’s left before Veiga’s effort is saved but Pepe was offside in the build-up.

Manchester City are dominating possession and perhaps it was a ploy by Enzo Marecsa to take it slowly and hog the ball in order to take the early sting out of Porto. The visitors would have been expecting the hosts would want to start hot so maybe they were willing to be slow on the ball in order to quieten down the crowd early doors. They have not had a shot yet and not really threatened the Porto goal but the hosts have not offered much going forward.

The weather in Porto really is horrible, the type of weather you would expect in Manchester in mid-November than Porto in early September.

Porto have a strong defensive record thus far this season but undoubtedly they will be tested a lot more tonight than they are in Liga Portugal. You would also imagine they will have to be clinical in attack as they are unlikely to create as many chances as they do domestically.

It has been revealed that with it hammering down, Porto boss Francesco Farioli has swapped his lovely suit that he was wearing pre-game for a tracksuit top and cap. At half-time, he will probably head back in drenched like all the players if he is active in his dugout.

We are under way at the Estádio do Dragão with the rain still teaming down in Porto. Manchester City’s Champions League campaign gets going.

It has been pouring down in Porto but that has not dampened the spirits of the home fans, who are in fine voice ahead of kick-off. The pyrotechnics have gone off and it is loud inside the Dragão. It has been a positive start for Unai Emery’s Aston Villa out in Belgium as they lead Club Brugge 3-1 at half-time.

Sources indicate that enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

According to recent reports, manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

“It is a hard place to come [Porto],” said Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that shows a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”.

Porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

It has been revealed that “We are going to face one of the significant favourites to win the competition,” Farioli remarked. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”.

Porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

Team news from Portugal to follow shortly.

Gli agenti hanno sondato i big: il Brentford ha chiesto Isaksen e la Juventus è pronta a offrire 40 milioni per Taylor.

Per la Lazio resta aperta la possibilità di operare nel mercato di gennaio a saldo zero, anziché subire un nuovo blocco totale. Lotito lavora da due mesi per trovare una soluzione. La decisione arriverà a dicembre dalla Commissione di controllo.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

In a recent development, A settembre il blocco invernale sembrava inevitabile, dopo gli acquisti estivi e la crescita del monte ingaggi. Ora nei conti biancocelesti si intravede uno spiraglio, seppure stretto. Lotito procede senza annunci, tra trattative, incastri e verifiche dei conti; a Formello restano prudenza e speranza.

La Commissione di controllo, che ieri ha firmato un protocollo d’intesa con la Consob, darà la risposta definitiva a dicembre. Fino a quel momento, l’ipotesi del saldo zero rimane aperta, ma non è una certezza.

Nel frattempo è pronto un piano alternativo. Gli agenti hanno sondato il mercato, raccolto offerte e valutato i major della Lazio. La linea del club, però, è quella promessa a Gattuso: nessuna cessione a gennaio.

Il Brentford ha chiesto Isaksen. Anche la Juventus potrebbe scontrarsi con la stessa posizione: è pronta a mettere sul tavolo 40 milioni per Taylor. La linea sulle cessioni è riassunta così: «In uscita non si muove nessuno». Almeno per ora, in attesa della decisione prevista prima di Natale.

"Secondo me ci sono giocatori buoni, intanto dico il blocco Premier, chi viene selezionato dalla Premier ha qualcosa in più e se non ce l'ha, poi la acquista. Ho messo anche Ahanor e Leoni. Ho preso anche i migliori di questa avventura, Bastoni, Scalvini, Dimarco ed Esposito e ho aggiunto anche Kean. Mi sembrano i due attaccanti più credibili, sarà difficile farli giocare insieme ma quando lo hanno fatto, Mancini ha fatto una scelta significativa e cioè Pio al centro e Kean intorno, un po' a destra e un po' a sinistra".

"Poi aggiungo le speranze: Tresoldi e Inacio sono due di talento, speriamo giochino per l'Italia. Ho messo due giovani sulla bocca di tutti: uno è Cassano che Mancini l'ha già convocato e l'altro è Mario Tambaro (classe 2012 del Napoli, ndr), se ne parla come di un fenomeno già a Napoli, ci sono già video che girano, lui che firma autografi, non ho paura di un infanticidio e non ho paura di rovinarlo ma voglio che questa diventi la missione dell'Italia: se c'è un talento, e Mancini è molto bravo ad indicarlo, va protetto, va allevato per il talento che uno ha: se uno è bravo palla al piede, lasciamoli la palla al piede, ci stanno mancando giocatori così".

Curtis Jones è pronto a scendere in campo. Ai box dal 19 settembre, il centrocampista inglese è ormai prossimo a tornare a vestire la maglia dell'Inter. Il risentimento miofasciale agli adduttori lo ha costretto a rimanere fuori due mesi e ha privato Cristian Chivu di un giocatore con caratteristiche uniche nella rosa nerazzurra. In vista del tour de force che attende i nerazzurri, l'inglese sarà fondamentale nelle rotazioni.

"La sosta nazionali è caduta nel momento migliore possibile, e in queste due settimane senza campionato Curtis ha approfittato per continuare a lavorare ad Appiano Gentile e riacquisire quella forma fisica che fin da subito aveva impressionato oltre che un po' di smalto. Certo, inevitabilmente mancherà il ritmo partita dopo la lunga attesa, ma a questo punto si tratterà solo di una questione di tempo e spazio", sottolinea la Gazzetta dello Sport.

"Un rientro che arriva nel momento migliore possibile, considerando che Zielinski tornerà affaticato dagli impegni con la Polonia, Barella e Sucic hanno giocato entrambe le partite con le rispettive nazionali da titolari, Calhanoglu un po' meno ma comunque più di un centinaio di minuti con la Turchia mentre Stankovic è rientrato dagli impegni con la Serbia direttamente infortunato. Il compito non semplice di trovare una collocazione a Jones starà così a Chivu, dentro un centrocampo che offre soluzioni e uomini diversi tra loro. Ma, si sa, aggiungere qualità non sarà mai un problema per un allenatore".

It has been revealed that “Quell’anima caraibica, che i nerazzurri hanno sperimentato nelle prime settimane con un po’ di stupore, sta curiosamente diventando un punto di forza: Djed Spence, inglese di Peckham, sud di Londra, ma con radici di famiglia piantate a Saint Mary, Giamaica, sta ribaltando il tavolo nerazzurro con la stessa leggerezza che all’inizio faceva preoccupare. L’esterno britannico con il mito di Bob Marley ha il sorriso costante e non la bava di un Lautaro, ma ha pure forza fisica e talento per dominare sulla fascia nerazzurra: da quando ha iniziato a prendersi una stabile titolarità, ha convinto tutti che quei 30 milioni siano stati spesi bene. Nel dettaglio, il pagamento è diviso in tre rate uguali da circa 10 milioni, si proseguirà a versare sia nel 2027 che nel 2028, più altri cinque di bonus legati agli scudetti, alle qualificazioni e ai risultati in Champions, quasi tutti subordinati alla partecipazione ad almeno metà delle partite”, sottolinea La Gazzetta dello Sport.

Sources indicate that “Nel trio di inglesi, Spence ha battuto i connazionali e non era scontato all’inizio: ha aspettato per cominciare a correre davvero a differenza di Jones e Stones, ora entrambi rientrati per la causa. Per Djed il ritardo iniziale nella preparazione e una squadra già costruita con un nuovo modulo hanno complicato il quadro. Ma ogni diffidenza iniziale è superata e Djed può definirsi ormai il titolare di Chivu: sorpassato il buon Diouf, che con Zizou trasloca ormai stabilmente a sinistra, mentre Luis Henrique, che avrebbe dovuto approfittare dell’attesa, vede restringersi pericolosamente lo spazio, con lo spettro del mercato di gennaio all’orizzonte. Il passaggio più evidente per Spence è stato a Rotterdam, dove ha ricevuto con stupore il premio di migliore in campo che l’Uefa gli ha messo in mano. Poi contro il Como ha elargito a Pio un altro assist, a testimonianza del filo teso con il centravantone rampante: sulla loro connection l’Inter promette di raccogliere altre reti. Giorno dopo giorno, anche Barella sul centrodestra di centrocampo si sta adattando ai suoi movimenti, diversi da quelli di Dumfries nell’ultimo quadriennio. In fondo, è solo questione di adattamento, tempo e pazienza”, chiude il quotidiano.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scegli Fcinter1908.it come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui.

Ospite dello Sport Industry Talk del Corriere della Sera, il presidente Beppe Marotta ha parlato dei problemi del calcio italiano:.

La storia dell'Italia, della FIGC ha dalla sua un palmarès ricco di successi e quindi una storia che ci rappresenta degnamente nel mondo. Tre titoli di campione del mondo non sono pochi. Evidentemente in questo periodo diciamo definiamolo un po' un periodo di involuzione, non abbiamo più partecipato agli ultimi mondiali e quindi questo è sicuramente un dato che ci deve far riflettere. Ma l'analisi sarebbe ampia. Il fatto che nel dopoguerra le squadre che andavano di moda erano quelle latine e soprattutto quelle danubiane, quindi l'Ungheria, la Cecoslovacchia, perché allora era la Cecoslovacchia, l'Austria. Dopodiché oggi vediamo che anche le squadre cosiddette parlo delle nazionali e poi anche dei club, cuscinetto, quelle che nella Champions sono terza e quarta fascia, oggi sono molto cresciute. Sono cresciute per due motivi secondo me. Hanno creato un modello dal punto di vista proprio calcistico, didattico allenatori sicuramente di grande prestigio. Secondo che hanno potuto attingere anche al reclutamento, quindi un bacino di reclutamento attraverso il fatto di tesserare i giocatori più facilmente rispetto all'Italia. Sono riusciti comunque a creare uno zoccolo duro di ragazzi e abbiamo visto il Belgio che veramente oggi sono all'altezza dei maggiori campioni in Europa, non a caso. Nel Belgio ci sono giocatori che giocano nelle più prestigiose squadre italiane. Prendiamo ad esempio la Svizzera. La Svizzera tra noi e la Svizzera c'era sicuramente un gap. Io ricordo che quando ero bambino abitando a Varese conoscevo abbastanza bene i giocatori della Svizzera, quantomeno quelli che erano nel canton Ticino. Bene, nella squadra di quel tempo era un portiere che nella vita normale faceva il postino. Oggi è impensabile una cosa del genere.

Quindi questo dimostra come anche il calcio si è evoluto, così come nella Champions League. Ci sono squadre come il Bodo per esempio che abbiamo affrontato l'anno scorso che oggi sono delle squadre che mettono in difficoltà anche i più grandi club. Quindi la difficoltà dell'Italia calcistica non nasce solo dal fatto che noi stessi siamo un attimino scesi di valore e di qualità, ma che le altre sono salite. Quindi la competitività va anche vista da questo punto di vista. Non a caso siamo stati eliminati negli ultimi due qualificazioni da squadre come la Macedonia e la Bosnia.

It has been revealed that per quanto riguarda l'appeal che il mondo della Serie A, o quantomeno il calcio d'élite dell'Italia, può dare sicuramente lo dà. Il fatto anche qui storico è che soprattutto nel Nord Italia, quindi Lombardia, Veneto, Piemonte, non c'è più quell'imprenditoria che c'era nel dopoguerra. Quindi sono venuto a mancare i cosiddetti mecenati, cioè quegli imprenditori che rivolgevano l'attenzione alle società calcistiche delle loro città e caso ultimissimo di Milano con Berlusconi e Moratti. E meno male dico che sono arrivati proprietari stranieri perché se non ci fossero state proprietà straniere, la maggior parte delle squadre sapete sono dei fondi, evidentemente il nostro calcio sarebbe ancora più in difficoltà. È evidente che le proprietà straniere vengono in Italia dopo che magari in alcuni casi hanno potuto valutare l'approccio con la Premier League che è il campionato diciamo più importante, ma lì i valori anche di acquisto dei club è nettamente superiore al nostro, per cui di ripiego poi vengono in Italia.

#26546. Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner

Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner

📅 09 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5474 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under new head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.
  • On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness.
  • And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under new head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a upcoming contract.

So, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face said it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

Mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

Sources indicate that mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W.

Sources indicate that there are certainly signs under Iraola, and following a difficult last campaign, that Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover the form he highlighted during his first two seasons at Liverpool. Time and again the 27-year-old made vital interventions, showed aggression and walked the tightrope of a harsh early yellow card. He dovetailed with Szoboszlai and that might be a concern for Gravenberch – watched by the Netherlands’ new head coach Xavi Hernández – if Iraola persists with this approach.

Although Mac Allister has two years left on his current deal, the last thing Liverpool need is yet another attention-sapping contract saga, even if he is not the same scale of player as Mohamed Salah or Trent Alexander-Arnold.

According to recent reports, for Iraola, after three Premier League games, comprising two draws and a victory over newly-promoted Ipswich Town, this will hopefully be lift off. A big European night at Anfield and coming from behind to beat one of the continent’s heavyweights.

“I loved it,” Iraola remarked, before castigating himself for misreading the way Atlético would line up. And what of Mac Allister’s riposte? There was a smile from Iraola before the Spaniard’s usual diplomacy kicked in as he talked about a “lovely, lovely goal” and how good it was for his midfielders to contribute.

Liverpool had to fight for it and what will have satisfied Iraola is that the defence, which has come under such scrutiny, held out. Even so, there are still serious concerns over the suitability of Milos Kerkez at left-back – who was badly at fault for Atlético’s goal – although the robust Ronald Araújo showed he can be a strong and versatile option on the other flank. The Uruguayan, signed on loan from Barcelona, is such a presence in both penalty areas and has the capacity to gain cult status.

According to recent reports, as does £123m signing from Paris St-Germain Bradley Barcola, who should have scored – once, certainly, possibly twice – and possesses astonishing pace that will undoubtedly lead to goals. There are also encouraging signs that his presence could enliven Florian Wirtz. Barcola eventually also went off, but thankfully it was only to cramp.

Sources indicate that there was a collective intake of breath across the Kop when Marcos Llorente was played through and bore down on them to give Atlético the lead. There was a desperate hope that he had strayed offside. There was then a realisation that Kerkez had, however, played him on with an appalling lack of awareness. Llorente beat Alisson.

It owed much to a wonderful shimmy, deceiving Szoboszlai in centre field, by Julián Alvarez before he smartly threaded the ball through, and Mac Allister’s international team-mate almost doubled Atlético’s advantage soon after. Only to be denied by Alisson.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc.

Industry observers note that we knew, we feared it would be Llorente who scored. Remarkably, he has now half of his 10 goals in this competition against Liverpool. Indeed, he named his dog Anfield after his extra-time brace knocked Liverpool, then the holders, out in the last 16 in 2020. And Liverpool had made a dog’s dinner of defending this time.

This is a different Atlético. A far less defensive, far more expansive Atlético. In years gone by, once they were 1-0 it was game over under Diego Simeone. But these days they try and play more and that gives their opponents a chance. And so it proved.

Recent findings suggest that atlético goalkeeper Jan Oblak did well to deny Barcola, with his trailing foot, before Wirtz won the ball back and found Szoboszlai who eventually ended the movement. It owed much, however, to a clever backheel to pick out the midfielder who finished low into the corner. Who executed that backheel? That would be Araújo.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY.

Barcola should have scored, sent clear by Wirtz in a brilliant, sweeping counter-attack, before Mac Allister did.

It has been revealed that the question now was whether Liverpool would show the resilience to see through the result. As Iraola made changes, they answered that with a resounding yes, which will have pleased him as much as the result, as much as the comeback, as much as Mac Allister’s stunning response.

In a recent development, “I was enjoying it [the Anfield crowd]. They [Atletico Madrid] are a very good team. Technically, in the middle, lovely players. It is not easy to press those players as they have quality. They have been playing together forever. We find another comeback after Nottingham Forest, after Newcastle. We still have this thing to improve in the beginning of the games, but I am happy as we have shown some character. This is the Champions League, you do not have easy games.”.

"You can see he's football mad." ⚽Steven Gerrard on Andoni Iraola's passion and the impact he's making at Liverpool 👏🎙️ @laura_woodsy | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M3qKhxt8HE.

There is the final whistle at Anfield and Liverpool start their Champions League campaign with a 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid. Liverpool did fall behind to Marcos Llorente’s goal but goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister give Andoni Iraola a win in his first Champions League game as a manager.

Victory in MD1 🤩 #UCL pic.twitter.com/SWFFhSudFJ.

Recent findings suggest that first Champions League game. First Champions League win for Andoni Iraola ✅ pic.twitter.com/D3CE6w6V0b.

Koumas is tripped by Le Normand and that should be it.

That is a silly foul from Lookman, with Frimpong inside his own box running back towards his own goal, but Lookman decides to push him in the back.

Just 60 seconds remain at Anfield.

There will be five added minutes.

It has been revealed that liverpool think they have sealed it through Frimpong but the offside flag has gone up. First Munoz cuts onto his right and has a shot saved by Oblak. The ball falls to Frimpong, who slots home but he was clearly offside when Munoz took the initial shot.

Kerkez is at the moment down with cramp and his night is done. He will be replaced by Tsimikas and Liverpool will make their final change at the same time. Koumas comes on for Isak.

It has been revealed that atletico win a corner but it all stems from sloppy play in the centre of the pitch from Gravenberch. He has had a few sloppy moments since coming on.

The corner is flicked on by Hjulmand but ends up coming to nothing.

Recent findings suggest that it isn’t the headline making performance, by any means, but that shouldn’t dilute the importance of Ronald Araujo’s contribution for Liverpool tonight and, indeed, against Ipswich last Friday. He’s doing what Liverpool wanted him to, providing versatility and leadership in their back four and - more than anything - quality. He hasn’t put a foot wrong.

In a recent development, atletico win a corner out on the left in front of their travelling supporters. Grimaldo’s outswinger is flicked on by the head of Hancko at the near post but it goes over.

Recent findings suggest that isak has the chance to potentially seal the victory for Liverpool but Le Normand makes a crucial block. Le Normand has only just come on but already made a couple of defensive actions.

Liverpool win a corner out on the left with the last touch coming off Pubill, who was marking Van Dijk from a free-kick. Szoboszlai’s inswinger is headed away by Le Normand.

Digeo Simeone is making his final two substitutions of the night as Le Normand and Hjulmad replace Romero and Barrios,.

Atletico bring on David, on loan from Juventus, for Baena.

Recent findings suggest that alvarez has a chance inside the Liverpool box but his shot is straight at Alisson. There are some appeals for handball but it hit Munoz from such close range that it is never a penalty.

Liverpool are making a substitution as Mac Allister, who scored the goal to put Liverpool in front, is replaced by Gravenberch. Mac Allister, who made some comments in the press conference yesterday about his sadness at not being offered a newly introduced contract, put in a good performance in the centre of Liverpool’s midfield. He was on a booking though so probably sensible to take him off when you can guarantee that the Atletico players would have tried to get him sent off.

In a recent development, we’ll see what happens in the coming weeks and months but there have been glimmers here with Florian Wirtz looking better than he has done with pace to pass to; if it clicks with him, Bradley Barcola & Alexander Isak it could be exciting but one game must be built on. It’s frustrating that Barcola’s night has ended with what appears to be cramp or tightness in his calf because he was getting more joy than he had done before half-time. The significant challenge for Liverpool, too, is whether they have the nous to see this contest out.

The new Netherlands boss Xavi is in attendance at Anfield tonight, watching the likes of Van Dijk, Frimpong and Gravenberch, although the latter is still yet to come off the Liverpool bench.

This is a concern for Liverpool. Barcola has gone down and seems to have some pain in his left calf. Is it cramp or an injury? It will be a double change for the home side as Frimpong and Munoz come on. Barcola is given a standing ovation as he goes off and the Liverpool fans will be hoping it is just cramp. Ngumoha also heads off.

Sources indicate that diego Simeone is going to make his first two changes of the night. Grimaldo and Lookman come on.

It is all Liverpool as they sense a third goal is there for the taking. Ngumoha does well down Liverpool’s left and pushes it past Pubill, who slides in and takes him down. Pubill is booked. He cannot believe it but I do not know why; a clear foul and yellow card.

That is a stunning strike from the Argentine. The ball falls to the midfielder just outside the box and he hits it first time. He hits the ball so crisply and there is nothing Oblak can do to stop it. Liverpool should have taken the lead through Barcola moments before they do now have the lead for the first time tonight.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W.

Well, that’s one way to prove you might warrant a latest contract. A quite beautiful left footed drive from Alexis Mac Allister gives Liverpool the lead and it has been noticeable thus far in Andoni Iraola’s matches that his team get stronger at the start of the second period. Diego Simeone most wonder how Atleti are losing a game they were controlling but Liverpool’s speed on the break is proving very good at causing chaos.

Barcola should have his first Liverpool goal and the hosts should be ahead but the Frenchman misses the target. It is the perfect counter-attack really from Liverpool and it is Wirtz and Barcola who exchange passes from deep inside their own half all the way to the Atletico penalty area. Barcola drives forward, into the Atletico box, and you think he is going to slot it into the bottom corner but his effort goes just wide. Barcola could and perhaps should have a brace tonight.

Barcola wins the first corner of this second half off Hancko right in front of The Kop. Liverpol take it short before Mac Allister clips the ball in. Araujo meets it and his header is powerful but it is off target.

Sources indicate that we are back under way at Anfield. No changes from either side at the break.

Some of the statistics are pretty even but Atletico Madrid have had just three touches in the Liverpool penalty area, yet have a goal to their name.

The first half at Anfield is brought to an end and it is level at 1-1 at the break. Llorente gave Atletico the lead before Szoboszlai equalised for Liverpool. The home fans let the officials know what they think of their performance in that first half.

One added minute at the end of this first half.

There has been about five minutes of squabbling between the Liverpool and Atletico benches, so much so that Tommy Elphick - Andoni Iraola’s assistant - missed Dominik Szoboszlai score the equaliser. Tensions have only increased after a nasty little challenge from Cristian Romero on Alexander Isak. The half-time whistle might be coming at a good time to defuse the situation but you fancy the walk back to the dressing rooms will be spicy.

According to recent reports, the conduct of the Atletico players is frankly embarrassing, not a massive surprise from a Diego Simeone side. Kang goes down clutching his face when there was barely any contact and then, unlike Isak, he does not have to spend a minute off the pitch.

Isak is on the ground, clutching at his knee, after a heavy challenge from Romero. It is a nasty challenge from Romero, who remarkably is neither booked nor penalised. To compound the awful officiating, Isak now has to spend a minute off the pitch owing to the upcoming rules. What do you make of that new rule of the player who is down going off for a minute? Have your say in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Moments after Liverpool equalised, Atletico have a decent opportunity to restore their lead but Baena drags his effort wide from the edge of the box.

Recent findings suggest that moments after Barcola could not take a massive chance to equalise for Liverpool, Szoboslzai does. First, Barcola is denied by Oblak. Liverpool keep it alive inside the Atletico box and a simple sensational flick by Aruajo finds Szoboszlai, who finds the bottom corner with a clinical finish. Kerkez has been poor tonight but he deserves credit for his part in that goal as he was the player to initially win it back for Liverpool with a good press.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY.

Liverpool look like a team that has been out of the Champions League for a couple of years and are only just finding its feet, which seems strange given they missed only one year in the last 10. They have glimmers of promise but they aren’t convincing anyone they will blow Atleti’s house down. One day everything will align for Atleti and they will reach another final. They have an outside chance this year, especially if Julian Alvarez - easily the best player on this pitch - has anything to do with it. Diego Simeone always has class strikers at the top of his team and Alvarez stands comparison with any who have gone before.

In a recent development, wirtz has a great chance to equalise for Liverpool but his shot on the half volley is saved by Oblak. It would not have mattered anyway had the ball ended up in the net because Isak was offside before crossing for Wirtz.

Some of the officiating tonight has been appalling and the latest example is VAR taking a check on a possible red card for Mac Allister for a foul that is never a red card in a million years. The officials then take an age to give yet another obvious offside and, in the end, the referee gives it rather than the linesman. That really does sum up the officials tonight as the referee should not be the one to give offsides.

In a recent development, alvarez shoots from distance and forces Alisson into a good save diving to his right. There was a suspicion of offside from Simeone in the build-up.

Atletico take it short but Simeone’s shot is blocked by Araujo.

What a save from Alisson! 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PuajED3Rks.

It has been revealed that the Anfield faithful are furious. Two fouls in quick succession are not given when they were both clearly fouls. The referee appears to have a different interpretation of body checks and taking people out off the ball than the rest of us.

Industry observers note that the Spanish side take the lead at Anfield and it is another goal on this ground for Llorente. Alvarez feeds a through ball to pick out the run of Llorente, who is onside. He takes one touch before firing past Alisson from the edge of the box. That is poor, poor defending from Kerkez, who not only played Llorente onside but then did not track the run properly. Llorente now has five goals on this ground.

Sources indicate that llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc.

The idea that Atletico Madrid are focused on spoiling and nullifying belongs in the past. They are an attractive team, well organised and you suspect they have the gears to cause Liverpool problems... and as we type, they have just opened the scoring by playing straight through Liverpool’s middle. It was a bad goal for home side to concede. Milos Kerkez was out of sync with the rest of Liverpool’s defence and Marcos Llorente has galloped straight through. As we remarked at the start: it’s a big test for the hosts... it’s just got even bigger.

A little line about Llorente, who has now scored five times against Liverpool in the Champions League. He is fond of playing in this arena, he named his dog “Anfield! when he bought it in 2021.

In a recent development, chance for Barcola. Szoboszlai clips a lovely ball in behind down the right channel to pick out the run of Barcola. The Frenchman takes it down beautifully before having his shot saved by Oblak. Barcola’s best moment thus far tonight.

Baena takes a first-time effort on from a central position around 25 yards out but he cannot keep his effort down and it sails into The Kop.

Industry observers note that atletico were renowned for years under Diego Simeone is being very tight at the back and in midfield, especially away from home. However, in recent years they have become more expansive and as a result are more open.

Sources indicate that liverpool win their first corner of the night at the Anfield Road End in front of the travelling Atletico fans. They take it short and Szoboslzai takes it towards the Atletico box. It appeared to be a very obvious foul on Szoboszlai right on the edge of the box but nothing is given. At the very least, it should have been given a free-kick as there was definitely at least one foul.

Barcola, who has won the Champions League with PSG in the last two seasons, is starting out on the right for Liverpool tonight with Ngumoha on the left.

Recent findings suggest that big test for Liverpool and it will be fascinating to see how this formation works out. It looks very much like it is 4-4-2, with Florian Wirtz almost alongside Alexander Isak and Rio Ngumoha the left winger and Bradley Barcola on the opposite flank - a position Andoni Iraola has referenced him playing in Lyon as a teenager. It’s also a big test for Iraola against Diego Simeone, the wily and vastly experienced manager, who is immaculately dressed - as always - in his trademark black suit.

Liverpool have a chance inside the opening minute. Szoboszlai wins it inside his own half and drives forward. He then plays it out to his right to find Isak, whose shot from the right side of the box is dragged wide of the far post. Isak did score from a similar position against Ipswich last Friday, when he scored at the near post.

A minute’s silence to remember the victims of the landslides in Nepal is impeccably observed.

We are under way at Anfield. Liverpool’s Champions League campaign gets going as Andoni Iraola takes charge of his first game as a manager in this competition.

Sources indicate that the two sides emerge from the tunnel to a cacophony of noise and we are moments away from kick-off at Anfield. The home fans boo the Champions League anthem and belt out “Liverpool! Liverpool!” over the top of it. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:.

The original “This is Anfield” sign has sold at auction for almost £150,000, 10 times more than its guide price.

The sign that hung above the players’ tunnel at Liverpool’s home stadium during the 1970s had been expected to fetch between £10,000 and £15,000 after being put up for auction on Tuesday and Wednesday.

But the “talismanic” piece of football memorabilia ended up being sold by auctioneer Budds for £149,500 to a UK private buyer.

The Argentine is into the final two years of his contract, which runs out in 2028. He arrived at Liverpool in the same summer as fellow midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, who have both signed new contracts. Mac Allister was linked with a move away from Liverpool during the summer transfer window and was candid about his contractual situation in the press conference yesterday:.

Industry observers note that “I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract which, of course, makes me very, very sad. Everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club every single day in training and games. Of course, I can have very good games [and] bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best.

According to recent reports, “I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it. At the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I did not get mine. Of course, there is still time. The fans do not need to worry because I will give my 100% until the last day I am here. There were options to leave this summer. I think right now I am in the right club and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club.”.

According to recent reports, former Liverpool manager Rafa Benitez, who led the club to Champions League glory on that famous night in Istanbul in 2005, is in attendance tonight. Andoni Iraola has just shared a hug with his compatriot and perhaps Benitez will have a few words of advice for Iraola ahead of his Champions League debut as a manager.

The Dutchman has been in fine form at the start of the season for Liverpool, registering a goal and three assists in his first three games. He missed training yesterday and is not in Liverpool’s matchday squad tonight. Andoni Iraola has confirmed that Gakpo has a small adductor injury that he picked up in the Ipswich game last Friday but could be fit for the weekend against Fulham.

When Liverpool won their sixth European Cup in 2019, they lifted it in the Wanda Metropolitano against Tottenham. This season’s Champions League final is in that very stadium and Liverpool’s Champions League campaign starts tonight against the club that plays their home games in that stadium, Atletico Madrid.

According to recent reports, “This is going to be a challenge, I hope, all the season because it would mean we continue in all the competitions. In this case, it is not the worst scenario because we played last Friday so we have had I think a good recovery. Probably it is going to be more difficult for next weekend, especially for the next game against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup because we will have just two days, game, two days, game. But we have to get used to this; it is what big clubs do. Definitely there is part of your mind where you have to think [about] the next games. But for us, the game tomorrow is very important.”.

According to recent reports, liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home as they host Atletico Madrid at Anfield. These sides met at Anfield on matchday one last season, with Liverpool winning a dramatic game 3-2. Liverpool led 2-0 inside the opening 10 minutes before Atletico came back to level the game at 2-2. Virgil van Dijk then scored in added time to give Liverpool all three points before Atletico boss Diego Simeone was sent off for clashing with the Anfield crowd, resulting in a one-match ban.

Andoni Iraola earned his first win as Liverpool boss on Friday night as they won 2-0 away at Ipswich thanks to a quickfire early double from Alexander Isak. This will be Iraola’s first Champions League match as a manager.

Recent findings suggest that “I think obviously it is a special night for me,” Iraola mentioned. “Everyone talks [about] the Champions League nights at Anfield and also the first game is against a strong opposition, it is Atletico Madrid. [Diego] Simeone is doing an incredible job as a manager. To be all the years that he has been achieving every season the goals of the club I think is remarkable and definitely it is a massive challenge for us. I think I played against him as a player, he was still a player, and I played against his teams when he was a coach and I also coached against him. So, we had a lot of precedent before. Definitely he has much more experience than me in this kind of games but I hope tomorrow we can give him a good game.

It has been revealed that “It is one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to position myself in the position that I am right now, and I hope I can enjoy it. It is a major responsibility, massive challenge, but I feel privileged to be there in that dugout tomorrow [tonight] and now my thinking is about putting the team together in a position where we can play a good game, win the game and start strong in this Champions League.”.

Recent findings suggest that atletico Madrid currently sit sixth in La Liga and suffered their first defeat on Saturday as they lost 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao. They did reach the semi-finals of the Champions League last season, where they fell to Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate.

“We are coming into a marvellous stadium and there will be a great atmosphere,” Simeone stated. “We will have to look good from the start of the game because it will be full on. He [Andoni Iraola] works very well with the team, focusing on the tactical awareness of each player. It takes time to find the right path, but he is growing and improving and he has some very good players.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Il Corriere dello Sport si sofferma su Sebastiano Esposito, attaccante di ventiquattro anni del Sassuolo e della Nazionale che piace da sempre al Napoli.
  • Recent findings suggest that I Am Naples Testata Giornalistica - aut.

Il Corriere dello Sport si sofferma su Sebastiano Esposito, attaccante di ventiquattro anni del Sassuolo e della Nazionale che piace da sempre al Napoli. Esposito, che può giocare sia da punta sia a ridosso del centravanti, sia da esterno, mostra una duttilità che lo rende utile in più sistemi e per tale motivo sarebbe funzionale alla squadra azzurra, in cerca di alternative in avanti. La convocazione in Nazionale e il rendimento con l’Italia hanno contribuito ad alzarne il valore, va inoltre sottolineato come il presidente Aurelio De Laurentiis lo avesse adocchiato personalmente tempo fa, insieme ai fratelli Pio e Salvatore, oggi rispettivamente all’Inter e alla Sampdoria. Il numero uno del club li voleva tutti e tre. Il Sassuolo ha preso Sebastiano in estate dal Cagliari in prestito con diritto di riscatto e per arrivare a lui bisognerebbe trattare con il club emiliano.

Martin Odegaard bails out comically wasteful Arsenal

📅 09 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5347 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For much of this sticky night in Naples, Arsenal appeared to be starting the newly introduced Champions League campaign the same way they finished the last one: by erroneously smashing the ball into the stands behind the goal.
  • Industry observers note that memories of Gabriel Magalhães’s ballooned penalty in the final against Paris St-Germain remain fresh in the mind, and here his team-mates were lining up to produce their own versions.
  • According to recent reports, thankfully for Arsenal, though, there was one player who was in no mood to relive the frustration of that shoot-out loss 14 weeks ago.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For much of this sticky night in Naples, Arsenal appeared to be starting the newly introduced Champions League campaign the same way they finished the last one: by erroneously smashing the ball into the stands behind the goal.

Industry observers note that memories of Gabriel Magalhães’s ballooned penalty in the final against Paris St-Germain remain fresh in the mind, and here his team-mates were lining up to produce their own versions. Bukayo Saka and Piero Hincapié, especially, delivered astonishing misses which were closer to entering orbit than the opposition net.

According to recent reports, thankfully for Arsenal, though, there was one player who was in no mood to relive the frustration of that shoot-out loss 14 weeks ago. Martin Odegaard has started this season in truly fabulous form and here he scored a truly fabulous late goal, fizzed into the corner from range, to cap another inventive individual performance and earn three points for his team.

Great play 😮‍💨Martin Ødegaard rounds off a wonderful passing move for Arsenal 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FrH6gW8Ak4.

In five matches this season, Odegaard has already scored four goals. That is three more than he managed in the whole of last season. The Arsenal captain is fit again and he is flowing. As ever, when Odegaard flows, Arsenal flow.

Sources indicate that “That’s what we need, the players with that mindset to decide the game and play with that personality,” said Mikel Arteta. “He has got that edge. He’s getting into those positions much more in recent games.”.

In the end it was a thoroughly deserved victory for the Premier League side, who were superior to Napoli in every department. Were it not for their comically bad finishing, they would have guaranteed the result long before Odegaard’s 75th-minute strike.

Their expected goals figure suggested they should have scored more than four goals, compared to Napoli’s 0.22. In total, they registered 26 shots – the most of any Arsenal team on record in a single Champions League match, and the most on record a Napoli team has ever faced.

Sources indicate that “With the amount of chances we generated, the scoreline has to reflect a very different result,” said Arteta. “The number of players that got into this situation, the amount of situations that we generated in various ways was something that pleased me a lot.”.

There was, almost inevitably, another clean sheet for Arteta’s side. They had the best defence in the Champions League last season, conceding only seven goals in 15 matches, and they were largely untroubled here. Ezri Konsa was once again excellent, in only his second start for the club. He successfully wrapped up Rasmus Hojlund, the former Manchester United centre-forward, and was as calm in possession as the absent William Saliba would have been. A potential injury to right-back Ben White was a concern, though.

According to recent reports, the Champions League is the one that Arsenal have never won and, you suspect, the one that Arteta really wants. Success in this competition would elevate Arsenal to a higher level as a club and fully establish Arteta as one of the great coaching minds of his generation.

It has been revealed that to lose last season’s final in such painful circumstances clearly hurt the Arsenal manager, who was visibly distraught after that shoot-out defeat despite the obvious delight of winning the Premier League title. If you could give him the choice between retaining the league this season or leading Arsenal to their first European Cup, he would surely pick the latter.

Arsenal have now won THIRTEEN UCL League Phase games in a row 🔴🔥 pic.twitter.com/UmcfMYO13r.

A trip to Naples in the first round of the league phase made for a lovely opening tie: atmospheric, intense and competitive. Napoli have had a difficult start to their campaign, losing two of three Serie A games so far, but they possess real quality and have a top manager in Massimiliano Allegri.

It has been revealed that even at the age of 35, the great Kevin De Bruyne still has power in his boots and schemes in his mind. When he tested Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya from range in the first half, it would have triggered horrible flashbacks in the minds of the travelling supporters. In his previous 17 starts against Arsenal for Manchester City, De Bruyne had scored eight goals and registered four assists. Thankfully for Arsenal, it was the only moment in which De Bruyne really threatened.

Throughout this game, Arsenal moved the ball around with precision and purpose. They created an extraordinary amount of chances, with Saka and Hincapié missing the best of them. Saka’s effort in the first half, when one-v-one with the goalkeeper, was strangely erratic. Hincapié’s opportunity, meanwhile, was laughable. Two yards out from goal, he somehow put the ball onto the running track that surrounds the pitch at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

Despite all the wasted chances, Arsenal kept going. Odegaard, in particular, kept probing. His goal was gorgeous: a swift exchange of passes between him, White and Christos Tzolis resulted in the Arsenal captain firing his effort from the edge of the area. Delicate build-up, ferocious finish.

Recent findings suggest that in keeping with the theme of the night, Arsenal should have scored more. Noni Madueke, for example, missed a one-v-one when it seemed like he had all the time in the world. But Odegaard’s intervention eventually proved to be enough, as he once again stood forward as Arsenal’s match-winner.

That’s all from us, but we’ll be back tomorrow night to bring you Man Utd’s return to the Champions League against Sabah!

"I think the chemistry, especially in the front players, has been exceptional." ✨Mikel Arteta tells @AnitaNnekaJones how impressed he's been by the connection between Martin Ødegaard and Christos Tzolis 🤝 pic.twitter.com/J6VOAMk4Lm.

Arsenal extend their #UCL unbeaten streak 👏 pic.twitter.com/wFBga6lNrN.

"We missed so many big chances"Mikel Arteta shares his thoughts after Arsenal's victory over Napoli 💭🎙️ @DannyJamieson | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zT2bHcPoiH.

Before all of that, Arsenal will now have to turn their attention to the Stadium of Light as they travel to Sunderland on Saturday.

They then face Ipswich Town in the EFL Cup on Tuesday night, before travelling to Brighton on the weekend.

Wed, October 21: Bayern Munich (A) 8pm.

Wed, November 4: Slavia Prague (A) 8pm.

Tue, November 24: Borussia Dortmund (H) 8pm.

Wed, December 9: Real Madrid (H) 8pm.

Wed, January 20: Real Betis (A) 8pm.

Sources indicate that “Everything runs through Martin Odegaard,” said Cole on TNT Sports. “He can stand still and find space. He is at the peak of his powers and it is beautiful to watch.

“You can’t help but love watching him play his football.”.

Plenty of praise for Martin Odegaard on TNT, with former Arsenal man Martin Keown heralding the captain’s behaviour.

“He’s setting an example to his players. He’s fitter, he’s hungry, and he did his talking on the pitch. He came good for his team.”.

It has been revealed that couple that with his impressive chemistry with latest arrival Christos Tzolis, and there is a lot of goal-scoring potential there this season. Three of the winger’s four assists have been for his captain, and we’re barely a month into the season.

The action has concluded around Europe tonight so here are your final scores from this week’s second night of European football:.

Possession: Napoli 42%-58% Arsenal.

Touches in opposition box: 9-52.

Napoli did not register a shot on target in that second half, and it is clear how much Arsenal just dominated to keep the pressure on.

It could easily have been three or four goals for Arsenal had they had better finishing, but either way, they did not let their heads go down.

It has been revealed that they kept pushing to see out the result and got the job done. Arteta will be very happy with that away result.

This has not been Arsenal’s most clinical performance but they got the job done.

Here is the goal that won it for them, courtesy of their captain:.

In a recent development, martin Odegaard has played some outstanding football tonight (again) and that is an absolutely outstanding goal. The delicacy of the build-up and then the ferocity of the finish. Four goals in five games for Odegaard this season.

Industry observers note that there will be alarm bells ringing for Allegri and Napoli, as they are heading for their third defeat on the trot. They have not created much of anything in this second half and you have to imagine that Arsenal will now make life very difficult for them.

To be exact, they have had a grand total of one shot in the second half.

Napoli will have to push now, and make more changes, bringing on Lorenzo Lucca and David Neres for Rasmus Hojlund and Stanislav Lobotka.

Guimaraes to Saka before the winger sends the ball back to Odegaard on the edge of the box. He lifts a ball into the centre of the box where there are a lot of bodies, but Tzolis snatches at it and sends the ball into the rafters.

Christos Tzolis and Bruno Guimaraes getting ready to come on.

Arsenal have only travelled to Naples once in the Champions League, back in 2013, which saw the home side win 2-0 and then Arsenal captain Mikel Arteta get sent off with two yellows. Arsenal still made it out of the group stages that year, helped by their own 2-0 win when the Italians came to N5.

“We know what this competition means to all of us, the experience of last year as well, so we need to start with the first game in a really, really tough place, but really excited to start the campaign.

Recent findings suggest that “It will be a really tough place, I’ve been in that stadium before, I know the atmosphere they create, their record at home is really, really strong. They have a very experienced manager, a lot of players that played in the league as well, so we know the challenge ahead. We are prepared and we’re ready to go.”.

Two matches kicked off at 5.45pm, and with just under half an hour to go:.

Recent findings suggest that the visitors are still without Cristhian Mosquera, who picked up an injury against Aston Villa, and Jurrien Timber – though the right-back has rejoined first-team training and travelled with the squad to Italy. William Saliba remains their only long-term absentee as he recovers from a back injury.

According to recent reports, naples have a few more players out of action. As well as McTominay, centre-back Alessandro Buongiorno is still sidelined following a knee procedure over summer and Andre-Frank Zambo Anguissa is missing with a groin injury.

Strikers Giovane and David Neres are dealing with hernia and knee problems respectively, while youngster Luca Marianucci is on his way back after a knee injury in pre-season.

Napoli have not started the season particularly well, losing two of their three Serie A games so far. But they do have a player who has a long history of hurting Arsenal: the great Kevin De Bruyne. The former Manchester City midfielder has been directly involved in 12 goals in his last 17 starts against Arsenal across all competitions (8 goals, 4 assists), including five in his most recent three (3 goals, 2 assists). Now 35 though, he is not the force he once was.

Here is how the hosts are lining up tonight:.

Meret; Olivera, Marin, Rrahmani, Di Lorenzo; De Bruyne, Lobotka, Gilmour; Santos, Hojlund, Politano.

Subs: Favasuli, Badiashile, Neres, Contini, Lucca, Vergara, Beukema, Milinkovic-Savic, Spinazzola.

Sources indicate that arsenal’s Champions League campaign last year ended in the most agonising of penalty shoot-out defeats but that should not detract from the brilliance of their run to the final. Mikel Arteta’s side were the only team who didn’t lose a single game in normal time in this competition last season, and also conceded only seven goals all season — the fewest of any team in the competition, despite the fact they played 15 matches.

Mikel Arteta has made four changes to the team that defeated Chelsea on Sunday. Piero Hincapie comes in for Riccardo Calafiori, Mikel Merino for Myles Lewis-Skelly, Eberechi Eze for Christos Tzolis and Viktor Gyokeres for Kai Havertz.

Both Aston Villa and Manchester City got off to winning starts last night, beating Club Brugge and Porto respectively. Other fun fixtures included Real Madrid beating Inter Milan, getting Jose Mourinho his own winning return in Europe with Madrid. Now it’s Arsenal’s turn.

After falling at the final hurdle last season – losing on penalties to Paris St-Germain in Budapest – they have travelled to the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona in Naples, hoping to take the first step of a new attempt to claim their white whale.

Their Italian hosts have not had the smoothest start to the 2026-27 campaign, settling under new manager Massimiliano Allegri. While Antonio Conte guided them to a second-place finish in Serie A last season, they have only managed one win from three league games – losing to Como and Inter Milan – meaning that they presently sit 12th in the league.

They were eliminated after the league phase of the Champions League last year, finishing to 30th out of 36 teams, and will surely be looking to improve on that poor performance this season.

Schalke goalkeeper Loris Karius has not ruled out a move to Bayern Munich, according to Sport Bild, who report that the 33-year-old could imagine himself becoming the No.2 to Jonas Urbig, with both Manuel Neuer’s (40) and Sven Ulreich’s (38) contracts set to expire in 2027.

Karius’ contract, though, doesn’t expire until 2028, meaning Bayern would have to negotiate with Schalke, who have no intention of selling their No.1 goalkeeper, who has received four Man of the Match awards this season upon the Royal Blues’ return to Germany’s top flight after a three-year absence.

Sky Germany earlier reported that there’s a 99.9 percent chance that Neuer will retire when his contract expires at the end of the season.

Should Karius move to Munich, he would “live significantly closer to his family, who live in Milan.” However, there are other names on sporting director Max Eberl’s shortlist, including Hoffenheim’s Oliver Baumann (36) and Lens’ Robin Risser (21).

After making his breakthrough with 513 minutes across eight Bundesliga appearances for Borussia Dortmund in 2025/26, Luca Reggiani has struggled for playing time this term with Die Schwarzgelben open to selling the Italian defender.

According to recent reports, the Italian defender was already a sales candidate in the summer, and has played just 27 Bundesliga minutes in 2026/27. As such, according to Ruhr Nachrichten, a departure in January is becoming “increasingly likely” with the Signal Iduna Park outfit setting their asking price at around €10m.

As reported in August, Reggiani has fallen down the pecking order following the arrival of Joane Gadou, while Italian compatriot Filippo Mane – who is currently sidelined through injury – has moved ahead of him. Because of this, the 18-year-old has found himself playing for BVB II in the Regionalliga West (fourth tier), as well as the UEFA Youth League as opposed to the UEFA Champions League, and the Premier League International Cup U21.

Borussia Mönchengladbach head coach Alexander Blessin has highlighted his strategy to get a result against unbeaten Borussia Dortmund.

The two Borussias clash in the Bundesliga on Saturday afternoon, with bottom club Gladbach in desperate need of a victory with just one from their opening nine.

In a recent development, “Dortmund obviously have enormous individual quality,” explained Blessin. “They have strong spells time and again, but there are also moments when you can get the better of them and perhaps right after the international break, that’s exactly when we can give them a hard time.”.

Industry observers note that relishing Saturday’s game, Blessin added: “We have to be highly focused and ready to give it our all for 90 minutes. It will be important to get away with it during the phases where Dortmund might have scoring opportunities or the upper hand. So that we can simply keep the game open until the 90th minute and then maybe score ourselves. It’s about having a high tolerance for suffering and showing the willingness to be really nasty.”.

Recent findings suggest that because Borussia-Park’s standing section has been increased, 54,909 fans will be in attendance on Saturday, beating the 54,042 record. “It’s going to be great,” added Blessin. “We’re looking forward to the game against a really good opponent, again whom we’ll give our all.”.

El Chadaille Bitshiabu (21) has played just 21 minutes for Galatasaray in 2026/27 following his summer loan move from RB Leipzig, and now the Turkish side could be ready to end the Frenchman’s loan deal.

BILD cite Turkish reports that Galatasaray are ready to send Bitshiabu back to Leipzig after arriving at the Süper Lig leaders in poor condition, reportedly 110kg and a body fat percentage of 18 percent – thus, he’s barely featured for Okan Buruk.

It’s important to note that Bitshiabu also takes up one of the foreign spots in Galatasaray’s squad, although BILD add that there have been no discussions between the two clubs regarding an early termination.

In a recent development, bitshiabu played 1,127 minutes across 21 Bundesliga games in 2024/25, but played just half that across 11 league games in 2025/26 under Ole Werner. Should the central defender return, then it’s likely that he will be shipped out on loan once again, with French outfit RC Lens one club that came close to signing the defender last summer, but that moved collapsed after both clubs failed to agree on the final conditions of the loan.

Vincent Kompany has lost only 12 of his 125 games in charge of Bayern Munich since succeeding Thomas Tuchel, but the Belgian tactician brings much more to Germany’s record champions than just a tactical nouse.

Sources indicate that speaking exclusively to t-mobile, Bayern president Herbert Hainer discussed Kompany’s approach. “Vincent Kompany truly brings a clear vision and a strong personality and, ultimately, it’s crucial what energy he unleashes in our team game after game. Through his approach, he consistently manages to forge a cohesive unit from our many individual world-class players. In February 2026, Kompany gave a 12 minute monologue addressing racism in football and strongly criticising José Mourinho’s reaction to the alleged racial abuse of Vinícius Júnior. Highlighting the Belgian’s importance as an ambassador for Bayern, Hainer added: “He himself emphasises that this speech arose spontaneously.

Speaking exclusively to t-online, Bayern president Herbert Hainer discussed the significance of Kane claiming the coveted prize, awarded to the world’s best footballer, for both him and Germany’s record champions.

“Harry has developed even further here. For him, it wasn’t just an award for one season, but for his achievements over the past few years – as a footballer and as a person. He’s a role model off the pitch as well. Furthermore, he’s shown that at Bayern, you can achieve anything individually.”.

Kane returned 73 games across all competitions for both Bayern and England last season, and he’s already in unstoppable form this term, plundering 10 goals and providing a further 10 assists in 15 appearances across all competitions for die Rekordmeister.

In a recent development, sul palco dello "Sport Industry Talk", evento organizzato da RCS, si è parlato anche di stadi del futuro. Il presidente dell'Inter Beppe Marotta a tal proposito ha detto:.

"Uno stadio nuovo deve rispondere ad alcuni concetti prioritari: deve dare senso di appartenenza, visto che è la casa di un club. In Italia, tutti gli stadi, tranne tre in Serie A, sono di proprietà o di enti comunali o del CONI nel caso di Roma. Questa è un'altra anomalia del calcio italiano. Deve rispondere anche a crismi di sicurezza, che oggi non ci sono più negli stadi; deve avere accoglienza e quindi dotarsi di ospitalità che va valutata a 360°, dagli sponsor al semplice tifoso che va in curva, sapendo che lo stadio è anche un contenitore di grandi emozioni. Un nuovo stadio di proprietà rafforza questi concetti. Non dimentichiamoci che è un asset di bilancio e, dunque, rappresenta un aspetto patrimoniale non da poco che può servire nella stesura del bilancio. Siamo anche in uno sport dove la competitività è fondamentale ed è garantita anche e purtroppo da disponibilità economiche per andare ad allestire squadre forti".

Recent findings suggest that "La differenza che oggi c'è tra noi e squadre come il Real Madrid nella valorizzazione degli introiti dallo stadio è ampia. Noi siamo arrivati a circa 100 milioni, e il Real Madrid è già a 300 milioni, con l'obiettivo di arrivare a 500. La disponibilità di questi ricavi può fare la differenza nell'allestimento della squadra. L'Italia da questo punto di vista è rimasta ferma: a fine anni '90 il bilancio della Juve, la prima in Italia, era di 57 milioni e il Real Madrid era addirittura dietro. Oggi il Real Madrid è arrivato a 1,2 miliardi, mentre l'Inter è arrivata a circa 500. Questo sta a dimostrare come anche le strutture hanno notevole rilevanza, anche nel concetto di sostenibilità".

Tech Report: Uli Hoeneß backs Jürgen Klopp to restore ‘hunger’ to German football

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that bayern Munich legend and honorary president Uli Hoeneß believes Jürgen Klopp can restore the discipline and hunger he feels have been missing from the German national team.
  • Industry observers note that “I think he will bring discipline and hunger back in,” Hoeneß stated.
  • Industry observers note that klopp’s Germany delivered their clearest statement yet on Monday night, thrashing the Netherlands 5-0 at Berlin’s Olympiastadion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that bayern Munich legend and honorary president Uli Hoeneß believes Jürgen Klopp can restore the discipline and hunger he feels have been missing from the German national team. Speaking at the Sport BILD Awards, Hoeneß backed the Germany head coach to impose his personality on the team while stressing that the rebuilding process will require patience.

Industry observers note that “I think he will bring discipline and hunger back in,” Hoeneß stated. “He is hungry himself. But I didn’t expect him to lay hands on everything to move quickly. We need to give him time. I also expect that many things will improve under Per Mertesacker, who is now overseeing the youth setup.”.

Industry observers note that klopp’s Germany delivered their clearest statement yet on Monday night, thrashing the Netherlands 5-0 at Berlin’s Olympiastadion. The emphatic victory secured top spot in Nations League Group A2 and a place in the quarter-finals, giving Germany a significant result as Klopp continues to reshape the national team.

In a recent development, hoeneß’s comments on hunger were not restricted to Klopp or the German national team. The 74-year-old argued that German football has been affected by broader social changes, recalling the environment in which he developed as a young player.

“I used to play football on the street after school, from two in the afternoon until nightfall,” Hoeneß noted. “That no longer exists today. We live in a country where most people are doing very well. I see this as the greatest danger for our football as well. If someone comes from Brazil, Portugal, or Argentina, they want to climb the social ladder. That is what we lack.”.

“We must learn again to work hard if we want to be successful,” Hoeneß continued. “That applies not only to footballers, but to the whole country.”.

For Hoeneß, Klopp’s task therefore extends beyond tactical adjustments or short-term results. The Bayern honorary president believes restoring the mentality he associates with successful German teams will be just as vital as the structural work being undertaken in Germany’s youth setup.

Rising Borussia Mönchengladbach star Wael Mohya (17) – who has scored two goals and provided one assist in nine Bundesliga games in 2026/27, and earned a call-up to Jürgen Klopp’s Germany squad – has featured in every league match for the Foals this season, launching himself into the limelight after making his top flight debut in December 2025. Now, the 17-year-old is attracting interest from Europe’s biggest clubs.

According to Sport Bild, Bayer Leverkusen are planning to meet with Mohya’s entourage with discussions with the player, his family, and Gladbach to follow. In addition to Leverkusen, Liverpool Bayern Munich, RB Leipzig and Brighton and Hove Albion are all interested in signing the youngster.

Recent findings suggest that mohya’s current deal expires in 2028 and while Gladbach want to extend the player’s contract beyond that, failure to reach an agreement could force their hand as they don’t want to lose the player for free in 2028. As such, a transfer fee in the region of €20m may be enough to entice Borussia, should they not be able to persuade the young attacker to extend his contract.
