FEATURE | Six winners from the Germany U21 November 2026 international break

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3847 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Getfootballnewsgermany

⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that antonio Di Salvo’s Germany U21s managed to conclude their 2026 calendar year with two consecutive friendly defeats during the November international break, falling 2-1 to Belgium in Essen before surrendering a second-half lead in a bizarre 3-2 loss to Croatia in Rijeka.
  • While such results certainly weren’t what Di Salvo and his staff had envisioned, the fact that neither result carried competitive consequences should temper the disappointment.
  • Industry observers note that the Belgium encounter featured some encouraging attacking football, particularly from players who had only recently entered or returned to the U21 setup.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that antonio Di Salvo’s Germany U21s managed to conclude their 2026 calendar year with two consecutive friendly defeats during the November international break, falling 2-1 to Belgium in Essen before surrendering a second-half lead in a bizarre 3-2 loss to Croatia in Rijeka. The results brought an abrupt end to an impressive eight-match winning streak and left the DFB youngsters with plenty to contemplate ahead of next summer’s UEFA European U21 Championship.

While such results certainly weren’t what Di Salvo and his staff had envisioned, the fact that neither result carried competitive consequences should temper the disappointment. Moreover, the international break wasn’t nearly as disappointing as the scorelines suggested. Our Get German Football News analysis of two matches yields just one fewer ‘winner’ than our long-form check on Jürgen Klopp’s senior men’s team.

Industry observers note that the Belgium encounter featured some encouraging attacking football, particularly from players who had only recently entered or returned to the U21 setup. The Germans repeatedly created dangerous situations through aggressive pressing, midfield combinations, and individual attacking initiative. Unfortunately, defensive lapses and insufficient precision in front of goal undermined much of the positive work.

Industry observers note that tuesday’s fixture against Croatia proved an entirely different proposition. Torrential rainfall, thick fog, and a playing surface that gradually transformed into something resembling a collection of small lakes made meaningful football almost impossible. Di Salvo’s team nevertheless recovered from a 1-0 halftime deficit to take the lead before the hosts scored twice in the final 25 minutes.

The conditions prompted the German U21 coach to question whether anything meaningful could be learned from the encounter. Speaking at the post-match press conference attended by Get German Football News, Di Salvo expressed relief that the players had escaped injury and emphasized that the earlier Belgium match offered a more useful opportunity for analysis.

There is another important consideration.

According to recent reports, the November squad had been weakened considerably by injuries and withdrawals. Established U21 contributors such as Tom Bischof, Lennart Karl, and Stated El Mala were also unavailable because of their involvement with Jürgen Klopp’s senior national team. The absence of captain Nicolo Tresoldi, who suffered a concussion in training, required Di Salvo to make significant alterations to his attacking looks.

The personnel difficulties opened opportunities for several players attempting to establish themselves at Germany’s highest youth level.

Some seized their chances rather emphatically.

Industry observers note that the author is thus pleased to present six winners from the November international break. The selections take account of individual performances, tactical contributions, and the extent to which players improved their standing ahead of next summer’s European Championship.

Industry observers note that few players entered November with more to gain than Cajetan Lenz. The 20-year-old made his Germany U21 debut against Belgium after previously earning nine appearances at U20 level and below. His promotion came at a particularly interesting stage in his club career.

Lenz emerged as one of the most impressive young midfielders in the 2. Bundesliga during his breakthrough campaign at Bochum, making 31 league appearances and attracting considerable interest from top-flight clubs. Get German Football News identified the youngster as a potential Bayer Leverkusen transfer target in its December 2025 transfer primer. Eintracht Frankfurt also pursued the midfielder before Hoffenheim ultimately secured his services.

The move has nevertheless presented some unforeseen difficulties.

Sources indicate that as GGFN examined following Lenz’s U21 debut, the midfielder has struggled to break into Christian Ilzer’s Bundesliga team, accumulating just three minutes of league football this season. His performances for Germany therefore carried particular significance. Lenz operated alongside Noël Aseko in central midfield against Belgium, contributing to several encouraging attacking sequences and repeatedly driving forward to support the team’s more advanced players.

Industry observers note that his energetic movement was especially key during Germany’s stronger first-half periods, when the hosts attempted to establish control through combinations involving Damar, Brunner, and the left-sided players. The debutant’s willingness to carry possession forward and participate in attacking movements offered an encouraging contrast to his limited opportunities at club level.

Industry observers note that di Salvo was clearly impressed. Speaking at the post-match press conference in Essen, the coach specifically identified Lenz as one of the players who had made a positive impression upon the coaching staff.

It has been revealed that “It’s a little early to discuss the [2027 UEFA U21] European championship roster,” Di Salvo remarked on Friday. “There are still many games to be played and many lads who, of course, aren’t here. And yet, there are some who – with their performances – have managed to make a mark with their impressions.”.

Industry observers note that “Namely, Cajetan Lenz, who played a very good game today,” Di Salvo continued. “He’s had very little playing time and I was thus pleased to see him log 85 minutes today. It was good that he could plow on through. From time to time he lacked clarity and the last pass was somewhat imprecise.

In a recent development, “But in general, he delivered a fantastic performance,” Di Salvo concluded. “He really ran a lot and marched forward. With that, particularly in light of his lack of playing time, we’re really satisfied with him.”.

Lenz followed his impressive debut with another encouraging appearance against Croatia. The Hoffenheim professional remained active despite the deteriorating conditions, nearly breaking into the penalty area early in the second half and heading narrowly wide from a Tom Rothe cross in the 51st minute.

Two minutes later, he provided the decisive touch from Damar’s free kick that enabled Moerstedt to score Germany’s equalizer. The youngster continued his attacking involvement throughout the second half, although he would undoubtedly have preferred a better outcome when Pejcinovic’s 82nd-minute shot rebounded into his path.

His failure to convert that opportunity represented one of Germany’s more frustrating moments during the final stages, but two consecutive 7/10 ratings constitute an impressive return for a player making his first two appearances at this level.

Recent findings suggest that lenz himself appeared determined to maintain realistic expectations when speaking to GGFN in the mixed zone after the Belgium encounter. The midfielder emphasized his gratitude for the opportunity while acknowledging that he remained a challenger for a regular position.

Di Salvo’s subsequent praise suggests that the youngster has already made considerable progress toward that objective.

According to recent reports, brunner’s inclusion hardly requires justification given his consistency across both matches. The former Germany U17 World Champion earned 8/10 ratings from GGFN against both Belgium and Croatia, emerging as one of the few German attackers capable of producing threatening moments throughout the international break.

Recent findings suggest that brunner’s November responsibilities were considerably different from those he had assumed earlier in the qualification campaign. As GGFN examined in its October Germany U21 Tactics Check, Di Salvo had previously enjoyed considerable success with a versatile attacking trio consisting of Brunner, Tresoldi, and Dzenan Pejcinovic. Tresoldi’s absence forced the coach to reconsider how best to organize his forwards.

Against Belgium, Brunner took on the central attacking assignment while Muhammed Damar moved onto the left. The Monaco professional began energetically and continued to involve himself in Germany’s attacking combinations, even if the hosts frequently lacked precision with their final deliveries.

It has been revealed that one of Brunner’s more notable contributions came in the 24th minute, when he drew the foul that provided Damar with the opportunity to equalize from a free kick. Brunner subsequently participated in the attacking sequence that resulted in Damar’s second effort against the crossbar in the 58th minute.

The youngster continued searching for a goal after Damar’s substitution, attempting an acrobatic finish in the 71st minute and producing several further incursions into the Belgian penalty area. The Croatia match offered an opportunity to demonstrate an additional dimension of his game.

Sources indicate that brunner began alongside Pejcinovic in what appeared to be a narrow 4-2-2-2. At halftime, however, Di Salvo introduced Max Moerstedt and deliberately shifted Brunner onto the left. The adjustment worked exceptionally well. Brunner became one of Germany’s most productive attacking players after the interval. His delivery for Pejcinovic’s 60th-minute goal supplied the visitors with a 2-1 lead, and the Monaco professional also struck the post during Germany’s strongest attacking spell.

Di Salvo deliberately and justifiably singled the 20-year-old out for praise after the break had officially concluded.

Recent findings suggest that while Brunner stands out for his consistency, Damar can reasonably claim to have delivered the outstanding individual performance of the international break. The Wolfsburg attacker returned to the U21 starting XI against Belgium following an extended absence and promptly produced a display worthy of GGFN’s Player of the Match award and a 9/10 rating.

It proved quite the joy to observe Damar’s stated determination to make the most of his national-team comeback manifest itself on the pitch. The 22-year-old began the first fixture shot out of a cannon and proceeded to cover nearly every blade of grass on the pitch. Beginning on the left wing, he frequently rotated into central areas and occasionally appeared on the opposite flank, creating considerable difficulty for the Belgian defenders attempting to track him.

His equalizer in the 25th minute was particularly memorable.

Industry observers note that having earned another opportunity from a dead ball, Damar cleverly drove his free kick underneath the jumping Belgian defensive wall. The technique was unusual, the execution excellent, and the subsequent celebration both touching and unforgettable.

According to recent reports, he wasn’t finished. A second free kick in the 38th minute was tipped onto the crossbar. He struck the woodwork again in the 58th following an excellent attacking combination with Pejcinovic and Brunner. There were stretches of the match during which Damar appeared determined to generate virtually every meaningful German attacking opportunity himself.

Speaking to GGFN and other journalists in the mixed zone afterward, Damar explained the instinctive decision behind his free-kick goal, expressed frustration about his missed opportunities, and spoke enthusiastically about the pride he takes in representing Germany.

His performance against Croatia was considerably less influential but that had much to do with the fact that the waterlogged surface made life particularly difficult for a technical attacker who relies upon close control, quick changes of direction, and precise passing. Damar nevertheless remained involved in Germany’s attacking moves and supplied the free kick from which Cajetan Lenz helped create Moerstedt’s equalizer.

The author still saw fit to award him a 6/10 in Rijeka.

Overall, Damar’s international comeback constituted an unequivocal success.

What a difference 45 minutes can make. Moerstedt’s November international break began with an unexpected call-up following Nicolo Tresoldi’s injury withdrawal and concluded with his first Germany U21 goal and a GGFN Player of the Match award.

The Hoffenheim striker only joined the squad after the international break had begun, making his U21 debut as an 86th-minute substitute against Belgium. There was little time for him to influence that fixture. GGFN awarded Moerstedt a 5/10, reflecting his brief involvement rather than any particularly poor performance.

Sources indicate that croatia presented a substantially greater opportunity. With Germany trailing 1-0 at halftime, Di Salvo introduced the youngster as part of a four-player substitution package. The coach wanted more presence inside the Croatian penalty area and consequently repositioned Brunner onto the left.

Moerstedt responded almost immediately. Germany emerged with greater attacking purpose, and the Hoffenheim striker began involving himself in combinations with the midfielders and his fellow forwards.

In the 53rd minute, Lenz redirected Damar’s free kick toward Moerstedt inside the Croatian penalty area. The striker’s initial effort was blocked, but he reacted rapidly enough to recover possession and convert at the second attempt.

The equalizer changed the direction of the match and helped establish the momentum that eventually produced Germany’s second goal. There was much to admire about Moerstedt’s performance beyond the finish itself.

The 20-year-old offered the type of physical presence and determination inside the box that Germany had lacked during the opening half. He remained available for deliveries despite the increasingly treacherous surface and helped occupy Croatian defenders as Brunner and Pejcinovic enjoyed greater freedom in attack.

Industry observers note that moerstedt’s first goal came in only his second U21 appearance, and his performance in Rijeka earned him an 8/10 rating. With Tresoldi expected to remain an important figure in Di Salvo’s aims, the competition for the central attacking position will undoubtedly be intense.

Moerstedt has nevertheless made an impressive opening argument for further opportunities.

Industry observers note that the next place goes to a midfielder who quietly delivered two of Germany’s more consistent performances during an otherwise difficult international break. Noël Aseko earned 7/10 ratings against both Belgium and Croatia, providing crucial energy and physical commitment in central midfield.

It has been revealed that aseko’s contribution deserves particular recognition because of the changes surrounding him. Di Salvo’s squad was missing several important midfield options, while the promotion of Tom Bischof to the senior national team and other withdrawals required the coach to assemble a revised central partnership.

Aseko consequently began both November fixtures alongside U21 debutant Cajetan Lenz. The pair faced an interesting challenge against Belgium. Germany wanted to press aggressively, regain possession high up the pitch, and support the attacking players through quick combinations. This frequently required the midfielders to advance into dangerous areas, leaving the defensive unit with considerable responsibility when the Belgians escaped pressure.

Aseko demonstrated his ability to carry possession forward as early as the sixth minute, accelerating past several Belgian opponents before combining with Brunner. His physical approach also produced an early yellow card, but the midfielder continued participating energetically in Germany’s attacking and defensive work. The partnership with Lenz was particularly encouraging.

Aseko contributed greater physicality and direct running, while his Hoffenheim colleague frequently assumed responsibility for progressing possession and connecting with the attacking players. In the Croatia match, with the playing surface progressively deteriorating, Aseko and Lenz were frequently required to abandon conventional passing combinations in favor of more direct and physically demanding actions.

Recent findings suggest that aseko nevertheless remained involved in Germany’s second-half revival. Immediately after the restart, the midfielder found himself in a shooting position following a corner, although his effort was blocked before reaching goal. His work helped Germany establish the territorial advantage that eventually produced Moerstedt’s equalizer and Pejcinovic’s second goal.

It has been revealed that aseko departed in the 64th minute, having again supplied an energetic performance despite the increasingly difficult conditions. Aseko continues to demonstrate why he deserves consideration for a regular place in that system. There are flashier candidates for an international-break winners list, but two strong performances alongside a newly introduced midfield partner merit recognition.

It has been revealed that the sixth and final inclusion requires a little explanation. Pejcinovic received a disappointing 4/10 rating from GGFN against Belgium, having struggled to impose himself consistently on the match. He nevertheless followed that performance with a considerably more encouraging display in Croatia, earning an 8/10 after scoring Germany’s second goal and producing several other noteworthy attacking contributions.

The contrast is interesting, particularly when considered alongside Di Salvo’s assessment of the Belgium encounter. Pejcinovic had already enjoyed an excellent qualification campaign before November. As GGFN documented following Germany’s decisive victory over Georgia, the Stuttgart professional scored twice to help secure direct qualification for next summer’s European Championship.

It has been revealed that his transfer from Wolfsburg to Stuttgart earlier in the season also represented an notable step in his professional development. As the striker acknowledged in an October interview , however, establishing himself at Bundesliga level for his latest club has presented challenges.

In a recent development, the November friendlies provided another opportunity to demonstrate his qualities. Against Belgium, Pejcinovic sometimes struggled with his timing and final deliveries. An attempted pass to Anton Kade early in the second half was particularly inaccurate, while his involvement in Germany’s attacking moves did not always translate into threatening opportunities.

There were nevertheless positive contributions. Pejcinovic helped initiate the 58th-minute sequence in which Brunner released Damar for another attempt against the crossbar. His movement and willingness to participate in combinations also provided Germany with an additional presence between midfield and attack.

Di Salvo was keen to emphasize these aspects when asked about the striker’s performance at the post-match press conference.

In a recent development, “No, that thought didn’t occur to me at all,” Di Salvo answered when questioned by the Rheinische Post about Dzenan Pejcinovic’s comparatively tepid performance on Friday night. “He trained strongly and scored his goals.”.

“We found him to be confident in the goal-shooting drills,” Di Salvo continued. “And we found the distance covered stats from not just Dzenan but the entire team today to be exceptionally good.”.

Industry observers note that “He was always running and strong on the press,” Di Salvo concluded. “That’s what I judge to be most important. That was good. He participated in the build up play in the first half and was able to help out the play on the wings. We found that well-executed by the entire team.”.

The coach’s comments provide a useful reminder that the assessment of an attacking player cannot rest exclusively upon his finishing or goalscoring contributions. Against Croatia, Pejcinovic offered considerably more of both.

An excellent opportunity went begging in the 18th minute after Damar released him into space, but the Stuttgart forward continued working energetically despite the difficult playing conditions. His perseverance was rewarded after Germany’s halftime adjustments.

With Brunner operating from the left and Moerstedt providing an additional penalty-area presence, Pejcinovic found himself benefiting from a more productive attacking structure. The Stuttgart professional finished Brunner’s cross in the 60th minute to give Germany a 2-1 lead.

Sources indicate that further contributions followed at both ends of the pitch. Pejcinovic helped defend two Croatian corners at the near post and continued seeking opportunities to threaten the opposition goal. His excellent shot from distance in the 82nd minute forced Toni Silic into a save, with the rebound presenting Lenz with an opportunity to equalize before Croatia’s eventual winning goal.

The 8/10 GGFN rating reflected a much more complete attacking performance.

Pejcinovic remains an vital member of Germany’s U21 squad, and November demonstrated both the value of his established attacking qualities and the considerable benefits of playing alongside forwards capable of complementing his movement.

Sources indicate that germany’s November international break offered plenty of interesting tactical material, even if the extraordinary conditions in Croatia necessarily limit how much one should attempt to extract from the second fixture. Di Salvo’s personnel difficulties were particularly significant.

According to recent reports, the absence of Tresoldi removed an established attacking reference point, while injuries and senior national-team promotions required substantial changes to the midfield and forward positions. The result was a Germany side that retained some familiar attacking principles but frequently looked different from the one that had secured European Championship qualification in October.

Germany began the Belgium encounter in a nominal 4-2-3-1, with Brunner leading the line, Damar operating from the left, Kade on the right, and Pejcinovic occupying the central attacking position behind the striker. Lenz and Aseko formed the central midfield pairing.

The basic structure proved rather fluid. Damar frequently moved away from his starting position, seeking possession in central areas and occasionally appearing on the right. Brunner and Pejcinovic also pushed together into advanced positions, temporarily giving the formation the appearance of a more conventional 4-4-2. The central midfielders were encouraged to advance and participate in Germany’s attempts to recover possession high up the pitch.

These movements helped produce several encouraging attacking sequences. The problem, unfortunately, concerned the spaces Germany left behind whenever Belgium managed to escape the initial press. Julien Duranville’s eighth-minute opener demonstrated the danger. Lucas Stassin beat Collins on the right and supplied the delivery that allowed Duranville to finish from close range.

In a recent development, the hosts subsequently established greater territorial control, but their commitment to attacking occasionally invited further Belgian opportunities. Collins’ misplaced pass in the 44th minute nearly produced another goal, with Stassin ultimately striking the post.

Di Salvo’s team appeared somewhat more cautious after the restart, although Damar’s movement and individual initiative continued to generate threatening situations. The final result nevertheless reflected Germany’s difficulties in balancing attacking ambition with defensive protection.

It has been revealed that belgium’s second goal arrived immediately after both coaches made several substitutions, with the German defensive structure unable to respond promptly enough to a newly introduced attacker. Di Salvo subsequently praised his team’s pressing at the post-match press conference but acknowledged that the defending and missed opportunities had not been good enough.

In a recent development, the Croatia encounter was considerably more difficult to assess. Di Salvo made just one starting change, replacing Collins with Linus Gechter in central defence. Poor visibility made the precise opening formation difficult to determine, although Germany appeared to operate in a narrow 4-2-2-2.

Sources indicate that the narrow attacking shape may have been influenced by the extraordinary circumstances. Thick fog made it difficult for players to locate teammates, while standing water increasingly disrupted attempts to circulate possession through the wider areas. The Germans initially attempted to play through the conditions, with mixed results.

Recent findings suggest that damar’s excellent pass to Pejcinovic in the 18th minute created a clear opportunity, but Croatia subsequently took the lead through Adrian Segecic. The most vital tactical development occurred at halftime. Di Salvo introduced Moerstedt, Collins, Morgalla, and Rothe. The changes allowed Brunner to move onto the left while Moerstedt assumed a more pronounced central attacking role.

Lineup—Germany U21 vs. Croatia (46th minute).

The adjustment immediately improved Germany’s attacking options. Moerstedt supplied the penalty-area presence necessary to capitalize upon deliveries and loose balls, while Brunner became considerably more influential when attacking from the left.

Lenz’s involvement in the equalizer illustrated the continued importance of Germany’s midfielders in supporting attacks, while Brunner’s cross for Pejcinovic’s goal demonstrated the increased productivity of the revised attacking arrangement.

The hosts’ subsequent equalizer, scored after the ball became stranded in a large puddle, served as another reminder that conventional tactical analysis has its limitations when the conditions become this extreme.

It has been revealed that the most encouraging developments concern Germany’s attacking options. Brunner demonstrated his versatility, Damar reaffirmed his attacking quality, and Moerstedt made an excellent initial case for a more substantial role in the U21 squad.

Pejcinovic remains a productive striker who can contribute beyond goalscoring, while Lenz and Aseko supplied an encouraging central midfield partnership despite the absence of several established alternatives.

In a recent development, the November defeats should not be dismissed, particularly given the defensive shortcomings that were evident against Belgium. Yet neither should the individual developments be overlooked.

Germany have already qualified for next summer’s European Championship, and Di Salvo now has several more footballers who have demonstrated that they deserve consideration when the competition for tournament places intensifies.

Two defeats, six winners, and more than a few selection headaches.

Not necessarily the conclusion to the international year one might have hoped for.

But certainly not a complete waste of time, either.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.

Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.

In a recent development, alonso’s side have shared 26 goals in the five games they have played this season. It has certainly been an entertaining start by Chelsea’s latest manager.

Palmer, Rogers and Pedro Neto stepped off the substitutes’ bench to complete a stunning rescue mission against Leeds United. Palmer scored twice, Neto once and Rogers helped himself to at least a hat-trick of assists. He claimed it was four, but the record books may say three.

In a recent development, when it was announced Palmer had been awarded the player of the match, Rogers responded by saying: “Mate, I got four assists. I can’t believe that! That’s mental. He scored a pen!”.

Industry observers note that "Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk.

Chelsea had looked down and out, when, just three minutes after Alonso’s quadruple half-time change, Leeds doubled their lead. But four goals in an incredible 12-minute spell turned the tie on its head and it was Alonso’s substitutes who Chelsea had to thank.

Sources indicate that palmer, with some help from Gillett, was the first to come to the home side’s rescue. Four minutes after Brenden Aaronson had put Leeds 2-0 up, Gillett pointed to the penalty spot after Daniel James had stood on the foot of Pep Chavarría.

Recent findings suggest that it looked like a harsh decision on Leeds and proved to be almost as big of a game-changer as Alonso’s substitutions. Palmer stepped up to score the resulting penalty.

Cole Palmer pulls one back for Chelsea from the spot! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/BUv6h1wTPQ.

In a recent development, “Nobody in the stadium, not one player was asking for a penalty and he gave the penalty,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, mentioned. “All of a sudden their players came into the game. The momentum was on their side. Situations can change the whole momentum of the game.”.

Stamford Bridge sensed a comeback and in the 55th minute, Rogers nudged the ball into the path of Palmer who produced a brilliant curling finish to beat Michael Zetterer, the Leeds goalkeeper.

That should have been that and the atmosphere could not have been more different from half-time, when Chelsea fans had booed off their side after watching them fall a goal behind.

Recent findings suggest that reggie Watson, Chelsea’s 16-year-old debutant, Malo Gusto, Estêvão Willian and Jamie Gittens were hooked at half-time by Alonso, who remarked: “For sure, I take responsibility for all of them. No player to blame. It’s the decisions that we took.

“I know that probably I haven’t taken the right decisions for them to show their best level. It’s something that I will analyse and learn from. So it’s my responsibility and we had to make decisions at half-time. And we have seen another second half with another quality.”.

Goalkeeper Mike Penders was one of the nine changes made by Alonso. He produced a superb double-save to first keep out Aaronson and then recover to tip Tarik Muharemovic’s header out from the corner.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of tonight’s Carabao Cup third-round tie between Chelsea and Leeds United. This is a rematch of last season’s FA Cup semi-final which Chelsea edged by a single Enzo Fernández goal, but plenty has changed since then. Xabi Alonso has taken over the reins at Stamford Bridge and made a promising start, reeling off three wins before losing to Arsenal in an absorbing contest last Sunday. Chelsea are not involved in European competition this season, so the domestic cups represent an avenue to silverware, as well as an opportunity to tinker.

It has been revealed that in Alonso’s way, though, stands a Leeds team whose manager, Daniel Farke, told the media on Tuesday that his side are aiming to win the Carabao Cup. Farke has overseen an impressive run of form, having lost only two of their previous 16 competitive matches in a stretch that extends back to March. Two wins at Nottingham Forest preceded draws against Brentford and Brighton to keep Leeds undefeated this term. Farke has suggested he will rotate in west London to “integrate latest players” having brought in seven new recruits during the summer.

If Leeds are to reach the next round, they must reverse a heavily one-sided head-to-head record against their hosts, who have won each of their past 10 cup meetings (three in the League Cup, seven in the FA Cup). In fact, Chelsea have lost at this stage of the competition just once in the past 15 years, and that was against Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City four seasons ago.

Sources indicate that alonso broke up the exhilarating “JP Morgan” band (João Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers) for Chelsea’s victory over Luton Town in the previous round, handing starts to Danny Welbeck and Estêvão. Players such as Jamie Gittens and Geovany Quenda are also waiting in the wings and may get chances to impress tonight. Mike Penders could also be in line for a start between the sticks.

Ospite dello Sport Industry Talk del Corriere della Sera, il presidente Beppe Marotta ha parlato di Oaktree e della doppietta dello scorso anno, ma anche dei bilanci in attivo dell'Inter:.

Oaktree? Secondo me è uno dei pochi casi in cui un fondo di investimento straniero arriva in Italia e non stravolge il management. La delega credo sia un grande atto di lungimiranza da parte della proprietà. Pur con la loro presenza quotidiana, perché sono presente sempre in modo molto silente e silenzioso, sappiamo che la proprietà c'è e con loro c'è un confronto. Questo è un atto molto importante. Abbiamo potuto creare e modellare quella che poi è stata un'Inter vincente. Se prendiamo in considerazione i risultati, lo dico con orgoglio e non con arroganza, nella stagione passata abbiamo vinto i due titoli italiani: il campionato e la Coppa Italia. Ci giocheremo la Supercoppa il 22 dicembre. Ma la cosa importante è che, per la seconda volta consecutiva nella storia del club, abbiamo chiuso il bilancio in attivo. Questo significa che, seguendo una determinata linea, si possono ottenere risultati sportivi senza esborsi così consistenti. È un dato di fatto: l'equazione secondo chi più spende più vince nello sport non è sempre valida. Spesso la competenza riesce a pareggiare l'investimento.

In un contesto in cui oggi il concetto di sostenibilità è una delle parole più abusate, anche noi dobbiamo comunque rispettarlo, perché sono le norme UEFA e quelle della Federazione che impongono il rispetto di determinati parametri economici. L'obiettivo del management è quindi quello di creare un mix tra il rispetto degli equilibri economici, finanziari e patrimoniali e il raggiungimento dei risultati sportivi. Questo va in controtendenza rispetto al calcio di una volta, quello in cui i grandi mecenati partecipavano alle competizioni con l'unico obiettivo di vincere. Poi, a fine campionato, andavano da quello che oggi chiameremmo CFO, ma che in realtà era il ragioniere, e dicevano: «Quanto costa?». Firmavano l'assegno e si ripartiva da zero. Oggi questo non è più possibile, innanzitutto perché le norme lo proibiscono e poi perché, giustamente, chi investe nel calcio vuole anche ottenere una certa stabilità, se non una vera e propria remunerazione.

It has been revealed that noi proseguiremo quindi con questo modello, fatto di investimenti. C'è un aspetto che entrambi noi abbiamo sottolineato: quello dello stadio, che rappresenta un investimento molto importante. Basti pensare che nel 2010 lo stadio di Torino è costato 500 milioni. Oggi noi stiamo affrontando un investimento da 1 miliardo e 300 milioni. Si tratta di un investimento privato molto pesante e significativo. E, riferendomi anche alla mia proprietà, gli investimenti non riguardano soltanto lo stadio, ma anche le strutture del club e quindi i centri sportivi, che sono fondamentali. Una delle altre carenze del calcio italiano è proprio la mancanza di centri sportivi di proprietà dei club. Ci sono ancora oggi società di Serie A che non dispongono di strutture adeguate al blasone della categoria. Anche da questo punto di vista voglio lanciare una denuncia e mi auguro che si possa arrivare a risolvere questo problema.

Dino Toppmöller, who left his role at French Ligue 1 side RC Lens in September, has been linked with a possible move back to the Bundesliga according to Sport BILD.

Cologne who only gathered nine points from the first nine games of the Bundesliga are contemplating a managerial change and the former Eintracht Frankfurt coach is on top of the list.

Toppmöller was dismissed from his role at Lens not because of results on the pitch but because of his loyalty to his assistant coach, whom he felt was wrongly terminated.

The Billy Goats will face Bayern Munich on Friday, but the next game against Elversberg on November 28 is expected to determine the future of 38-year-old coach Wagner.

Toppmöller was under consideration in Cologne last summer, but an agreement wasn’t reached on his salary. According to Sport Bild, the 45-year-old would be open to renewed talks. In addition to Toppmöller, Christian Eichner (most recently at Karlsruhe), Horst Steffen (most recently at Werder Bremen) and David Hubert (Union Saint-Gilloise) are possible candidates for the role if Wagner departs.

Industry observers note that il Corriere del Mezzogiorno si sofferma sulla chiusura del bilancio del Napoli che al 30 giugno 2026 ha realizzato un utile di 2,2 milioni in virtù del ritorno in Champions, definendo questo aspetto “una boccata d’ossigeno anche per il mercato di gennaio, tenendo conto dei parametri e della condizione dell’organico, con il rischio di non avere gli introiti della partecipazione alla Champions nella prossima stagione e senza plusvalenze di grande spessore da poter immaginare. Conquistare il passaggio ai play-off in Champions e risalire la classifica in campionato non sono solo obiettivi sportivi ma anche percorsi rilevanti sotto il profilo economico. Giocarsi dei traguardi che portano incassi significativi potrebbe spingere il Napoli ad anticipare le trasformazioni dell’organico che dovranno essere compiute in estate”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Il prossimo 14 dicembre la FIGC procederà con le elezioni del nuovo presidente.
  • Il commento di Simonelli sul duello Galliani-Malagò per le elezioni in FIGC: "Ogni competizione elettorale è sempre un momento delicato, ma può essere anche un momento o di continuità o di rilancio.

Il prossimo 14 dicembre la FIGC procederà con le elezioni del nuovo presidente. Una seconda volta dopo quelle di giugno e dopo che la federazione, da poco nelle mani di Giovanni Malagò è stata commissariata proprio con lo stesso Malagò scelto come commissario. Questa volta ci sarà molta più concorrenza, tutta risiedente nel nome di Adriano Galliani che ha avanzato la sua candidatura. In merito a questo duello ha detto la sua Ezio Maria SImonelli, presidente di Lega Serie A, nel corso dello sport talk organizzato questa mattina da RCS.

Il commento di Simonelli sul duello Galliani-Malagò per le elezioni in FIGC: "Ogni competizione elettorale è sempre un momento delicato, ma può essere anche un momento o di continuità o di rilancio. Non è un segreto che undici club della Serie A hanno appoggiato la candidatura di Giovanni Malagò, e quindi sarà questa sfida tra due colossi del mondo dello sport: Giovanni, che credo abbia dato prova, con le sue presidenze al CONI, di grandi successi per lo sport italiano, dall'altra parte Adriano Galliani, sostenuto da alcuni club di Serie A – tre di Serie A hanno espressamente firmato per lui – e dai calciatori e dagli allenatori, che è comunque una persona che è tra i più accreditati nel mondo del calcio, tra i dirigenti più esperti. Quindi, comunque, è una sfida, come dico, tra colossi. Il ruolo mio, come presidente di Serie A, è quello soprattutto di dialogare con le altre componenti, perché quello che è l'obiettivo – chiunque vincerà le elezioni, a cui faccio entrambi gli auguri – è poter avere delle componenti unite per poter lavorare sul futuro del calcio che, come avete visto, si sta facendo qualcosa, ma c'è ancora molto da fare. Quindi in bocca al lupo a Giovanni, in bocca al lupo ad Adriano, e che vinca il migliore".

Una doppietta nella goleada contro il Perù. La partita di Robinho jr nel Brasile Under 20 si può sintetizzare anche così. Una prestazione importante per il giovane neoacquisto del Genoa nella sessione estiva di mercato. Ha lasciato il segno così come lo ha fatto nella formazione Primavera rossoblù e come spera di farlo anche in prima squadra dove mister Daniele De Rossi gli ha già dato una chance a gara in corso nel finale del match dell'Olimpico contro la Roma.

Sogna Robinho jr, figlio dell'ex stella fra le altre anche del Milan, sogna anche la nostra Nazionale. Nel post gara, riporta Globo Esporte, il ragazzo non ha chiuso la porta ad un'eventuale chiamata azzurra: "Tutti sognano di giocare per la propria Nazionale. Io ne ho due e sono entrambe le benvenute. Ovviamente, il mister ha detto che conterà su di me e quindi sarò disponibile".

According to recent reports, E il prossimo anno ci sarà il Campionato Sudamericano Under 20 campionato a cui il giocatore spera di prendere parte: "Le convocazioni le fa l'allenatore e dipendono sempre dal momento. Io non posso dire di avere già un posto in squadra. Lavorerò molto duramente con l'obiettivo di ricevere la convocazione per il torneo".

Mainoo looks primed for battle with Man City’s new-look midfield

📅 11 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4672 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.
  • After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.
  • Little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.

After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.

Little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range. Otherwise, it was one-way traffic.

United’s biggest threat on the night was complacency, but there was none of that. This was a professional, unfussy display with a few nice flourishes. Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq.

Industry observers note that “It’s nice to keep a clean sheet and obviously win the game,” Carrick mentioned. “Some of the football we played was really good – dangerous on the transition. The result looks comfortable, but it wasn’t always like that but we did a lot of good things.

United probably could not have asked for a softer return to Champions League football. Atlético Madrid at the Wanda Metropolitano next month will certainly be a very different beast, but it was a rewarding first 45 minutes all the same that paved the way for Carrick to ring the changes ahead of the derby.

Already leading 1-0, two goals shortly before the interval changed the complexion of the game and effectively extinguished any flickering hopes Sabah had of a gargantuan upset.

Founded just nine years ago, Sabah had navigated four qualifying rounds that began on July 7 just to reach this stage.

Throw in the fact Valdas Dambrauskas, their Lithuanian manager, got his break in coaching with the Manchester United Soccer Schools 20 years ago, and it is quite the heartwarming tale.

But there is not much sentiment at this level and, given time and space, United punished their inexperience and carelessness.

Carrick will not read too much into the performance. City will be an entirely different proposition and it will be interesting to see whether he goes for a two-man midfield with Bruno Fernandes deployed as an advanced No 10, or perhaps operates with a midfield three and adjusts his attack.

Either way, Mainoo will be central to the game plan.

It is hard to believe the England midfielder missed most of pre-season after reporting back late following the World Cup, because he has barely missed a beat in his last three outings, even if his team-mates have not always hummed to his tune.

There is so much to like about Mainoo. His manipulation of space, how he never looks under duress, even when hounded, and his vision on the ball. There was one lovely angled ball over the top here, after United had worked the space well, that released Fernandes in behind. His cross was cut out before Sesko could tap in.

Mainoo’s work off the ball has improved enormously, too. There were numerous instances here of him making a timely intervention or nicking the ball away at the right moment to recover possession.United have spent £155m reconfiguring their midfield, but Mainoo will be a constant. “He’s a fantastic player, it’s pretty obvious to see,” Carrick noted. “He has a massive influence on our games. He is a real joy to have, he wants to improve, he wants to listen and it’s great to see.”.

Kobbie Mainoo completed 81/83 passes, 6/6 accurate long balls and 10 passes into final third on his full Champions League debut ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/NK9BIGvc4m.

It will certainly be interesting to see how Carrick’s newly introduced-look midfield shapes up against City’s own revamped one in the form of Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Sources indicate that “There are some good connections and we have played some good football through the middle of the pitch,” Carrick added. “A lot of it is on wavelength and understanding of where each other wants the ball. We haven’t had the perfect start but there are really good signs.”.

According to recent reports, carrick was suitably confident to withdraw Youri Tielemans at half-time and bring on Mason Mount, who was having a good pre-season before his familiar injury jinx hit, and he will have been pleased to see Sesko on the scoresheet again. “He definitely offers a different kind of threat,” Carrick noted. “There are not many who can give us what Ben does with his physicality, playing on the last line. It’s great to have him back.”.

Sesko’s goal, rounding the goalkeeper to slot home from Bryan Mbeumo’s pass after line-breaking balls from Mainoo and Fernandes, capped off a quick-fire three minutes when Sabah were unpicked. Before then, Cunha had picked out Tielemans’s burst into the penalty area, from where he pulled the ball back for Fernandes to coolly finish.

Benjamin Šeško rounds the goalkeeper to make it three for Manchester United 🔄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tnslugsmZM.

Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans combine to double Manchester United's lead ✌️📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nZnkwLWJ00.

United had taken the lead when Kaheem Parris paid the price for a misplaced pass straight to Mbeumo, from which the ball was moved at pace between Sesko, Fernandes and Patrick Dorgu to tee up Cunha to score.

Sources indicate that dorgu was starting here at left-back with Shaw rested with one eye on City. It was an early glimpse of how Carrick is going to have to manage the minutes of his only recognised senior left-back, who is not going to be able to play every few days.

Carrick prefers Dorgu further up the pitch and it remains to be seen if he trusts the Dane at left-back in bigger games than this.

With City having played in Porto on Tuesday and had a little extra rest time, the United manager will have been pleased he got the chance to withdraw several key players early. He was even able to give a rare run-out to Joshua Zirkzee and it was the Dutchman who helped to force the fourth goal.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q.

Sources indicate that fernandes’s quick free-kick caught out Sabah and Zirkzee back-heeled the ball goalwards. It bounced off Aden McCarthy and from there goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov got himself in a dreadful spin, unable to locate the ball by which point Martínez had blasted it in from a yard out.

Job done. Now a much bigger test awaits.

Industry observers note that “Nice to have a clean sheet and obviously win the game. Some of our attacking play was fantastic. We were dangerous in transition, defended well in the most part. The result looks comfortable but it was not as easy as that. Kobbie [Mainoo] is a fantastic player, it is pretty obvious to see. He has a massive influence on our game and a real joy to have. Through the middle of the pitch, we have played some good football at times and we can get better. There are some good signs which we have shown tonight. The confidence is there, like at Everton on Sunday for large spells, just took a hit there at the end with the result. It is always nice to win. Another substantial one on Sunday.”.

The final whistle is blown at Old Trafford and Manchester United claim a 4-0 victory on their return to the Champions League. Goals from Cunha, Fernandes, Sesko and Martinez give Michael Carrick’s side three points in their opening game of the competition. Debutants Sabah return home with nothing and no goals, despite some decent chances to get a goal.

A number of empty seats at Old Trafford are becoming visible as some home fans have seen enough, knowing their side is going to win.

Sabah have had a few chances to come away from their Champions League debut with a goal but have wasted some great chances, including one just now. Mickels delivers a lovely cross from the left, which perfectly picks out Mbina, but his header goes just over the bar.

There will be three added minutes.

Mickels wasted a glorious chance in the first half and he comes close to goal a now but drags his shot just wide of the far post from the left side of the box.

According to recent reports, how on earth have the officials missed that one? Cunha catches Almeida on the leg and it should be at least a booking but the officials do not see it, despite the linesman being not far away. Cunha is very lucky as that was a nasty challenge.

Sabah would love to at the very least send their travelling fans back to Azerbaijan with a goal on their Champions League debut. You do wonder how different the game could have been had Mickels not missed a sitter that would have seen Sabah make it 1-1.

Michael Carrick is going to make his final two changes of the night as youngsters Lacey and Amass come on.

In a recent development, A bit of a soft goal for Sabah to concede. Fernandes clips in a free-kick into the Sabah box which picks out the run of Zirkzee. The Dutchman’s backheel is blocked and Sabah should then deal with the danger. However, Sabah make an absolute mess of things and their keeper Pokatilov has no idea where the ball is, allowing Martinez to nick in and smash the ball into the net.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q.

Lepinjica is the first Sabah player into the book tonight for a cynical trip on Mount.

Zirkzee, only just on the pitch, shoots from range but it is straight down the throat of Pokatilov.

Puchacz takes the free-kick from just over 25 yards out and strikes it well but the effort is just off target.

Perhaps with the Manchester derby on Sunday in mind, Michael Carrick is going to make a double change. Zirkzee and Santos replace Sesko and Mainoo.

Dorgu is the first player into the book tonight. Lepinjica spots the run of Parris into the right channel and plays a clever pas forward. Dorgu cynically brings Parris down and is rightly booked.

The visitors are making a change as Parris is replaced by Isaev.

Industry observers note that manchester United come close to a fourth and Cunha his second. The home side work it well near the Sabah penalty area with a couple of clever flicks and passes before Cunha has an effort saved by Pokatilov to his left.

Recent findings suggest that mazraoui receives it out in space on the right and cuts inside onto his left. He comes across the face of the penalty area before getting his shot away but his effort is off target.

Sabah are enjoying a decent spell of possession but have not yet threatened Lammens’ goal in this second half.

It has been revealed that is Yoro lucky? Mickels appeared to turn him not far outside the Manchester United penalty area but Yoro is not penalised. It did on first viewing look like a foul and would have been at least a yellow card.

We are back under way at Old Trafford. How quickly might Michael Carrick make changes with Sunday’s Manchester derby in mind? Well, he has made one change at the break as Mount replaces Tielemans. It is Mount’s first appearance of the season. Sabah have brought on Mbina at the break.

Those two goals late in the half completely change the complexion of the game and Michael Carrick’s half-time team talk. Good first 45 minutes back in the Champions League for United.

Possession: Manchester United 59%-41% SabahShots: 14-4Shots on target: 5-0Corners: 6-2Touches in opposition box: 35-4.

In a recent development, the first half is brought to an end and Manchester United are cruising towards victory on their return to the Champions League. It has all gone wrong for Sabah.

That is game, set and match before half-time at Old Trafford as the dam has burst for Sabah. Sesko is played in behind by Mbeumo and is one-on-one with Pokatilov. Sesko takes it around Pokatilov before putting it into the empty net.

Benjamin Šeško rounds the goalkeeper to make it three for Manchester United 🔄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tnslugsmZM.

Michael Carrick’s side have their second of the night not long before half-time and it is a well-taken goal. Cunha, from the left side of the box, plays it inside to Tielemans. The Belgian takes one touch before, on the turn, playing it back into the path of Fernandes, who finds the net with a first-time finish.

Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans combine to double Manchester United's lead ✌️📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nZnkwLWJ00.

Fernandes has an effort from the edge of the Sabah box but blazes his effort high over the bar.

That’s a warning there for United. Fernandes gives the ball away in the middle with a heavy touch and Sabah break through the tall, languid figure of Lepinjica. Parris’ cross loops the far post where Mickels should have done better than steer an inviting header into the side netting. Bit of a let off for Carrick’s side.

Sabah should be level as they miss a sitter. Parris, from the right side of the box, clips a cross to the back post that picks out Mickels. He should score but puts his header into the side netting. That should have been the equaliser for Sabah.

Dorgu clips in a cross from the left side of the box and picks out Sesko, whose hooked first-time effort goes just wide.

Half an hour in and United have been in command. It’s not scintillating but they warrant their lead and punished a misplaced pass by Parris brutally. Mainoo is orchestrating the game in the middle of the pitch. Best player on the park so far.

Parris’ shot from the edge of the box takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner. It is wasted though by Sabah as the inswinger is easily caught by Lammens.

Tielemans steps in with a crucial interception inside his own box to deny Mickels the chance of a shot on goal.

The Brazilian has his first Champions League goal but it is gifted by Sabah. The visitors are threatening a counter-attack but Parris inexplicably gives the ball away on halfway with a dreadful pass across the pitch. The ball is then moved out to the left, where Dorgu crosses. He picks out Cunha, whose first-time effort with his side foot hits the Sabah keeper Pokatilov and goes into the net. A sense of frustration had been growing inside Old Trafford but Sabah have rather gifted Manchester United the opener there.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq.

Sabah give it away inside their own half and Manchester United flood forward towards the Sabah penalty area. Mbuemo drives forward and cuts inside onto his preferred left foot before getting his shot away from the edge of the box but it is straight at Pokatilov.

That is outstanding defensive work from Dasdamirov. Mainoo plays a quite sensational first-time ball in behind into the right channel to pick out the run of Fernandez. The Manchester United captain has Sesko waiting in the middle for the cross but Dasdamirov steps in with an absolutely essential interception or else Sesko would have had a tap-in.

Sabah need to be careful as now a few times they have been caught in possession deep in their own territory.

Cunha sends in a corner from the left that threatens to go in at the far corner but Sabah keeper Pokatilov catches it near his own line.

Sabah are making their Champions League debut and so too tonight are Cesc Fabregas’ Como, who have just taken the lead at home against RB Leipzig. Manchester United will travel to Como in late October on matchday three. Manchester United play RB Leipzig at home on matchday six.

It has been revealed that sabah have to negotiate a couple of Manchester United corners in quick succession and they do so. The visitors’ starting XI tonight has a very international feel to it:.

Michael Carrick has made four changes for Sabah to the team that drew 2-2 against Everton. Benjamin Sesko is given his first start of the season with Marcus Rashford dropping to the bench. Luke Shaw was given an additional rest day on Wednesday and is left out of the squad. It makes sense with Sunday’s derby against Manchester City to come but it’s an early glimpse of the delicate balance Carrick will have to strike with his only recognised senior left back this season. Shaw can’t be expected to play every few days given his history of injury problems.

It looks like Patrick Dorgu will be operating at left back against Sabah. This is United’s 300th fixture in the European Cup, including qualifiers. On the subject of qualifiers, Sabah became only the sixth side to navigate four qualifying rounds to reach the European Cup proper, with their campaign starting back on July 7. That was the same day Argentina beat Egypt in the last 16 of the World Cup. The Azerbaijan club were only formed nine years ago so have had quite the ascent since.

At 8pm on Thursday night, Manchester United will kick a ball in the Champions League for the first time in three seasons.

According to recent reports, it must mark the start of a permanent return to Europe’s premier club competition. If United are serious about once again challenging for the Premier League title and building a £2bn stadium, that must be the way forward.

This is only the seventh time in 13 campaigns that United have been in the Champions League and the implications have been significant.

Presenting your Champions League Reds 📋❤️‍🔥.

In a recent development, manchester United make their return to the Champions League as they host tournament debutants Sabah of Azerbaijan on matchday one at Old Trafford. It will be the first time that Manchester United have faced an Azerbaijani side in European competition.

Recent findings suggest that manchester United have one win, one loss and one draw to their name in their opening three Premier League games. They were seconds away from winning their second game of the season on Sunday but conceded a late equaliser at Everton. They last featured in the Champions League during the 2023/24 season, when they were eliminated in the group stage, and have won just one of their last nine games in the competition.

Industry observers note that “It means an awful lot [to be back in the Champions League],” Manchester United boss Michael Carrick said. “Challenging yourself against the elite, the very best. This football club has been used to being the best. It is not something you can take for granted. We missed out on it for a number of years and now we are back. It is where we expect to be without getting ahead of ourselves. We have made huge steps to make it in, now it is about pushing into the next chapter and evolution if the squad and this is certainly where we want to be.

“I do not think it is a case of if we get to a certain stage it is a success and if we do not it is not. We have to embrace the fresh challenge that we are facing as a group and push to what we can push to. If we get further down the line in this competition then who knows? I am not writing anything off. But we are taking it step by step and we certainly are not getting ahead of ourselves. We have got a squad that is strong enough to compete.”.

Sources indicate that sabah make their Champions League debut having been founded just eight years ago in September 2017. Back in April, they secured the Azerbaijan top-flight title for the first time in their history and also won the Azerbaijan Cup in May. They earned a spot in the Champions League group stages after beating Hapoel Be’er Sheva 6-4 on aggregate. In the previous three seasons, they have tried to reach the group stages of the Europa and Conference Leagues but failed to do so. They have won all three leagues thus far, including a 5-0 home win over Zira last Saturday.

Dopo la pausa per le nazionali, la Serie A è pronta a ripartire e il Milan si prepara a tornare in campo davanti al proprio pubblico. Domenica, a San Siro, i rossoneri ospiteranno il Frosinone con l'obiettivo di dare continuità agli ultimi risultati e consolidare la propria posizione in classifica.

Recent findings suggest that la squadra riparte dal quarto posto, a sole cinque lunghezze dalla vetta, ma soprattutto dalla ritrovata fiducia dopo due vittorie pesanti, prima nel derby e poi a Genova. Due successi che hanno rilanciato le ambizioni milaniste e che ora attendono una conferma: la sfida contro il Frosinone dirà se si è trattato del vero punto di svolta della stagione. In questo articolo analizziamo le quote Milan vincente Serie A dopo le prime undici giornate e le prospettive dei rossoneri nella corsa allo Scudetto.

È passato il primo quarto del campionato, il Milan procede bene con 7 vittorie, 3 pareggi e una sola sconfitta che al momento valgono il quarto posto in classifica. Le parole del proprietario Gerry Cardinale alla vigilia del derby sono state inequivocabili: "Credo al 100% che il Milan possa vincere lo scudetto quest'anno". E ha promesso invrestimenti anche nel mercato di gennaio per dare al confermatissimo Ruben Amorim una squadra ancor più competitiva.

Recent findings suggest that È ancora presto per tracciare un bilancio definitivo sulle ambizioni di questo Milan, ma le prime undici giornate offrono già indicazioni importanti. Un rendimento che inevitabilmente si riflette anche sulle quote Milan vincente Serie A, aggiornate dai bookmaker alla luce dei risultati più recenti.

Sources indicate that la squadra da battere resta l'Inter, reduce dal ventunesimo Scudetto della propria storia. I nerazzurri di Cristian Chivu vengono proposti a 1,65 e mantengono quindi un vantaggio molto netto sulle inseguitrici. La principale alternativa è attualmente la Roma di Gian Piero Gasperini, che si trova intorno a quota 4,50, mentre il Milan si colloca nella fascia 11-15.

Sources indicate that il gruppo delle possibili contendenti non termina però qui. La Lazio di Gattuso oscilla indicativamente tra 10 e 15, mentre il Como, con 23 punti nelle prime undici partite, continua a essere considerato l'outsider più interessante, anche se la sua vittoria del campionato paga fino a 18 volte la posta.

According to recent reports, le quote fotografano una Serie A nella quale l'Inter parte ancora avanti, ma alle sue spalle non esiste al momento un'unica anti-Inter nettamente riconoscibile. Il Milan vuole inserirsi proprio in questo spazio e la vittoria nel derby della Madonnina ci fa capire che la qualità complessiva della squadra è alta. Ora, però, sarà necessario dare continuità ai risultati, cosa che fin qui è mancata.

Con undici giornate già archiviate, il torneo si prepara ad affrontare un finale di 2026 ricco di appuntamenti da cerchiare in rosso sul calendario. Dalla 12ª alla 19ª giornata, infatti, non mancheranno gli scontri diretti, le sfide tra piazze storiche del calcio italiano e gli incroci che potrebbero contribuire a ridisegnare gli equilibri della classifica prima della sosta natalizia.

A presentarsi all'appuntamento con il finale d'anno da capolista è il Palermo, che guida la graduatoria con 27 punti, quattro in più rispetto al Modena. Alle loro spalle ci sono Ascoli (20) e Mantova (19), mentre un gruppo composto da Hellas Verona, Avellino, Benevento e Pisa insegue a quota 16. Una situazione che rende particolarmente interessante il calendario delle prossime otto giornate.

It has been revealed that il primo appuntamento da evidenziare è quello del 20 novembre, quando l'Hellas Verona ospiterà il Cesena. Il giorno successivo toccherà invece alla capolista, attesa dalla trasferta contro il Catanzaro. Sempre il 21 novembre riflettori puntati anche su Empoli-Pisa, altro confronto tra due società che hanno ambizioni e storia da massima serie. Il turno infrasettimanale successivo, la 13ª giornata, proporrà ulteriori incroci di grande interesse. Il 24 novembre il Palermo ospiterà il Sudtirol, mentre il 25 novembre andrà in scena Pisa-Modena, confronto particolarmente significativo tra una delle inseguitrici e la seconda forza del campionato. Da seguire anche Cesena-Ascoli, con i bianconeri marchigiani attualmente nelle zone alte della graduatoria.

Il calendario non concede pause neppure nelle giornate successive. Il 28 novembre il Palermo riceverà il Benevento, mentre nello stesso pomeriggio l'Empoli affronterà l'Hellas Verona. Il giorno successivo spazio a Sampdoria-Cremonese, altra partita fra due realtà che hanno conosciuto recentemente la Serie A e che puntano a ritrovare un ruolo da protagoniste. La 15ª giornata, in programma nel weekend del 4-6 dicembre, metterà invece di fronte Pisa e Sampdoria, con appuntamento fissato per il 4 dicembre. Ma soprattutto proporrà un confronto di grande richiamo come Hellas Verona-Palermo, in programma il 6 dicembre. Una partita che potrebbe avere un peso importante anche nella corsa al vertice, con la capolista chiamata a misurarsi con una delle piazze più ambiziose del torneo.

L'8 dicembre, in occasione della 16ª giornata, riflettori puntati su Sampdoria-Modena, mentre il giorno successivo il Palermo ospiterà la Cremonese. Due incroci di assoluto interesse, con i rosanero chiamati a difendere il primato e i canarini impegnati in una trasferta che potrebbe dire molto sulle loro ambizioni. La giornata successiva, in programma il 12 e 13 dicembre, proporrà un altro appuntamento da non perdere: Cesena-Palermo. I siciliani saranno quindi attesi da un altro confronto impegnativo lontano dal Barbera. Nello stesso turno spiccano anche Sampdoria-Vicenza e Modena-Catanzaro, due partite che coinvolgono società dal passato importante e con obiettivi differenti nella stagione attuale.

According to recent reports, prima della pausa natalizia, il calendario riserva ancora diverse partite di richiamo. La 18ª giornata, prevista tra il 18 e il 20 dicembre, proporrà Hellas Verona-Cremonese, Benevento-Pisa ed Empoli-Sampdoria, oltre ad Ascoli-Modena, altro confronto significativo per la parte alta della classifica.

Il gran finale arriverà però con la 19ª giornata, in programma il 26 e 27 dicembre. Il programma propone infatti Modena-Palermo, scontro diretto tra le prime due della graduatoria, ma anche Sampdoria-Hellas Verona e Cesena-Pisa. Tre partite che potrebbero regalare indicazioni importanti prima della pausa e della successiva ripartenza del campionato, fissata per il 9 gennaio.

Otto giornate, dunque, nelle quali il campionato potrebbe assumere una fisionomia ancora più definita. Palermo e Modena avranno diversi scontri diretti da affrontare, ma alle loro spalle Ascoli, Mantova e le altre inseguitrici proveranno ad approfittare di ogni possibile passo falso. La Serie B si prepara a vivere un finale d'anno intenso, con un calendario che promette spettacolo e punti pesanti in palio.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scegli Fcinter1908.it come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui.

Intervistato da La Gazzetta dello Sport, l'ex difensore della Lazio Nestor Sensini ha parlato della squadra di Gattuso in testa alla classifica:.

«La mia Lazio, dovete dire. Io sono un po’ della Lazio, un po’ dell’Udinese e un po’ del Parma. Alla Lazio ho conquistato il mio scudetto. Quell’esperienza si è appiccicata alla pelle, la festa di un popolo intero. Come si fa a dimenticare una cosa così?».

Questo è il passato, e del presente che cosa dice?

«Che la Lazio può fare il bis».

In a recent development, «Ha tutte le qualità per centrare l’impresa. C’è l’ambiente giusto, un allenatore come Gattuso che trasmette una grinta incredibile e non è mica uno sprovveduto dal punto di vista tattico, e poi c’è un gruppo che, partita dopo partita, si rende conto di essere competitivo. Perché non bisognerebbe credere alla possibilità di conquistare il titolo?».

La concorrenza per lo scudetto, però, è notevole. C’è l’Inter, c’è la Roma e non solo.

«Allora, cominciamo con il dire che se la Lazio riuscisse a centrare l’obiettivo, sarebbe una specie di miracolo sportivo. I mezzi finanziari non sono paragonabili a quelli degli altri club, e qui bisogna fare i complimenti a tecnici e dirigenti che hanno individuato gli elementi giusti per il progetto che aveva in testa Gattuso. Poi, certo, l’Inter ha qualcosa di più a livello di rosa, come qualità e quantità. E pure la Roma. Però là davanti c’è la Lazio, e con pieno merito. Nove vittorie, due pareggi e zero sconfitte: il cammino è fantastico. Ho un solo dubbio».

«Prima o poi arriverà una sconfitta e bisognerà vedere come il gruppo reagirà alla caduta. Ma sono convinto che Gattuso saprà come affrontare anche i momenti negativi. L’importante è che l’ambiente si stringa sempre attorno ai ragazzi ».

«Non sono un indovino, però per quello che ho potuto vedere e per i risultati che ha messo in fila, la Lazio lotterà fino in fondo. Lo ripeto: questa squadra ha il carattere del suo allenatore, e avete mai visto Gattuso mollare nel corso di una gara? Lo stesso dovranno fare i suoi giocatori, e mi sbilancio: alla fine, ce la faranno. E io sarò a festeggiare con loro».

L’Inter si prepara a ripartire in campionato e non solo. Domenica l’Atalanta, poi un calendario fitto di impegni. Per fortuna Chivu ha ritrovato forze importanti durante la sosta.

Industry observers note that “La coppia Esposito-Thuram ha così la possibilità di aprire la sfida di Bergamo, con Lautaro pronto a cambiare ritmo a gara in corso. Non è ancora abbondanza, perché Bonny resterà fuori per diverse settimane. Esigenza, appunto, e il derby ha palesato quanto l'Inter sia più fragile, lungo i novanta minuti, senza alternative soprattutto offensive. Il vero nodo resta l'infermeria. Nelle prime quindici gare stagionali, l'Inter ha accumulato 37 assenze-partita per infortunio: un peso sulla continuità del lavoro”, scrive il Quotidiano Sportivo.

In a recent development, bonny e Stankovic, fermato da una lesione all'adduttore durante gli impegni con la Serbia, sono i casi che richiedono più tempo. Akanji, tornato affaticato dalla Svizzera, non preoccupa; Zielinski, alle prese con un fastidio alla pianta del piede, va ancora valutato al rientro dalla Polonia. Segnali incoraggianti arrivano invece da Stones, Curtis Jones e Luis Henrique, recuperati, mentre Pavard è nuovamente utilizzabile. Per Chivu, significa poter ricostruire rotazioni vere anche dietro e in mezzo al campo. Sarebbe semplicistico attribuire la lunga catena di problemi muscolari a una sola causa.

“Calendario fitto, nazionali, viaggi e recuperi sempre più compressi spiegano parte delle difficoltà, ma obbligano anche a ragionare sulla distribuzione dei minuti sull'intensità del lavoro. L'Inter deve inseguire risultati senza consumare troppo in fretta chi è appena rientrato. Sono nove gli appuntamenti in trentuno giorni, tra Cham-pions e Supercoppa: ogni recupero diventa prezioso. Con magari l'aggiunta di benzina di una fumata bianca nelle trattative di rinnovo con Hakan Calhanoglu. Il ritorno di Lautaro restituisce una cer-tezza. La sfida di Chivu è fare in modo che non diventi l'ennesima presenza a intermittenza. Ma che sia la tanto attesa risposta ad un'urgenza”, aggiunge il quotidiano.

Senza Zaccagni, Gattuso prepara Noslin sulla sinistra; Frattesi si è allenato in gruppo, ma resta il dubbio sul suo impiego.

Andrea Pinamonti giocherà per la prima volta da titolare all’Olimpico con la Lazio nella sfida di sabato contro il Lecce. Secondo quanto riportato da La Repubblica, L’assenza di Zaccagni gli darà ancora spazio al centro dell’attacco, con Noslin sulla sinistra al posto del capitano. Per il centravanti è un’occasione per cercare il terzo gol in biancoceleste.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Industry observers note that pinamonti sa di non aver ancora conquistato i tifosi laziali. La fiducia di Gattuso nei suoi confronti, racconta La Repubblica, alimenta però la sua voglia di riscatto e può aiutarlo a sbloccarsi anche dal primo minuto.

Nelle due precedenti gare iniziate da titolare, a Udine e Napoli, il numero 9 arrivato in estate non ha convinto. È stato sostituito nella ripresa, rispettivamente al 52’ e al 61’. Sabato spera che la prima partenza dall’inizio in casa segni un cambiamento.

Proprio all’Olimpico, entrando nel secondo tempo, ha segnato i suoi due gol con la Lazio. Il colpo di testa contro il Cagliari è stato decisivo; il piattone del 3-1 contro il Monza ha chiuso una partita rimasta fino a quel momento in bilico. Ora Pinamonti va a caccia del tris.

In a recent development, contro il Lecce, Noslin prenderà il posto di Zaccagni sulla fascia sinistra, mentre Pinamonti agirà al centro. L’intesa tra l’attaccante italiano e l’olandese è ancora da affinare, ma Gattuso è convinto che la formula possa funzionare.

Il tecnico ha ricevuto segnali positivi anche da Frattesi. La mezzala ha svolto con il gruppo il primo allenamento settimanale. Il lavoro in squadra non scioglie ancora la riserva su un suo impiego dal primo minuto contro il Lecce, ma cresce l’ottimismo sulla sua presenza.
