Recent findings suggest that il Milan fa sul serio e prepara un autentico colpo da novanta per il mercato di gennaio, riportando in cima alla propria lista dei desideri il nome di Endrick. Dopo aver dovuto desistere nella scorsa sessione estiva di fronte alla chiusura totale del Real Madrid, la dirigenza rossonera - intenzionata a investire subito a titolo definitivo senza ricorrere a formule in prestito - ha già avviato i primi contatti concreti sia con il presidente Florentino Perez sia con l'entourage del talento brasiliano classe 2006. Lo riferisce Sports Brazil: lo scarso minutaggio fin qui raccolto dall'attaccante classe 2006 e la necessità di garantirgli maggiore continuità anche in ottica Brasile sono punti a favore per il Diavolo.

Secondo le indiscrezioni di TNT Sports Brazil, il Milan sarebbe pronto a mettere sul piatto una proposta complessiva da 70 milioni di euro, strutturata su una base fissa da 60 milioni più altri 10 milioni legati ai bonus. Sul piano contrattuale, il club di Via Aldo Rossi sarebbe aperto a ritoccare verso l'alto l'attuale ingaggio del giocatore, superando i 3,2 milioni di euro netti a stagione percepiti oggi a Madrid. Per tutelarsi dal rischio di perdere definitivamente il controllo sul giocatore, i Blancos vorrebbero inserire nell'accordo un diritto di recompra fissato tra gli 80 e gli 85 milioni di euro - esercitabile nell'arco di due anni - oltre a una clausola di prelazione per pareggiare eventuali future offerte provenienti da altri top club europei.

Sources indicate that L'ostacolo principale tra il Milan ed Endrick resta però rappresentato dalla posizione di José Mourinho. L'allenatore portoghese continua a considerare il centravanti brasiliano una risorsa preziosa nelle rotazioni del Real Madrid e non vorrebbe indebolire la rosa a stagione in corso. Eppure, lo Special One non può trattenere il giocatore controvoglia. Molto dipenderà dalla posizione espressa dal 20enne.

It has been revealed that I biglietti per la sfida di martedì 22 dicembre alle ore 21:00 allo stadio Giuseppe Meazza saranno disponibili solo in formato digitale su smartphone con QR code. Si potranno acquistare esclusivamente su Vivaticket. Per acquistare bisogna accedere alla piattaforma, registrarsi (se non si ha già un account) e completare l'ordine.

Biglietti Supercoppa, i settori riservati ai tifosi dell'Inter.

Ai sostenitori dell'Inter sono riservati i settori Verde, suddivisi in questo modo:.

It has been revealed that FASE 2 – TUTTI GLI ABBONATI SERIE A 2026/27Da mercoledì 18 novembre dalle ore 15:00 alle 23:59 si aggiungono tutti gli abbonati Serie A 2026/27, compresi quelli di Secondo Verde. Ciascuno potrà acquistare fino a 4 biglietti in qualsiasi settore dello stadio, a condizione che tutti gli intestatari siano abbonati.

In entrambe le fasi, per ogni biglietto bisogna inserire nel campo codice coupon il numero della tessera Siamo Noi (12 cifre), seguito da "-" e dalla data di nascita in formato GGMMAAAA (es.: 007000000000-GGMMAAAA).

In a recent development, FASE 3 – SOCI INTER CLUB PLUS 2026/27Da giovedì 19 novembre dalle ore 12:00 alle 23:59 si aggiungono i soci Inter Club PLUS 2026/27 attivi al 17 novembre compreso. Ciascuno potrà acquistare fino a 4 biglietti, a condizione che tutti gli intestatari siano soci Inter Club PLUS.

FASE 4 – SOCI INTER CLUB BASE 2026/27Da venerdì 20 novembre dalle ore 12:00 alle 23:59, in base alla disponibilità, si aggiungono i soci Inter Club BASE 2026/27 attivi al 17 novembre compreso. Ciascuno potrà acquistare fino a 4 biglietti, a condizione che tutti gli intestatari siano soci Inter Club BASE.

Nelle fasi 3 e 4, per ogni biglietto bisogna inserire nel campo codice coupon il numero della tessera Inter Club, seguito da "-" e dalla data di nascita in formato GGMMAAAA (es.: S0000000000-GGMMAAAA).

VENDITA LIBERALa vendita libera degli eventuali biglietti residui partirà mercoledì 2 dicembre alle ore 12:00 e sarà riservata a chi paga con Bancomat Pay. Da giovedì 3 dicembre alle ore 12:00 si potrà pagare con tutti i metodi di pagamento.

Sources indicate that PERSONE CON DISABILITÀDa mercoledì 9 dicembre alle ore 12:00 e fino a esaurimento posti, i tifosi con certificato di invalidità al 100% che necessitano di assistenza continua (la condizione deve essere indicata sul certificato) potranno richiedere i biglietti a loro riservati. L'accompagnatore deve essere maggiorenne.

Di seguito i prezzi stabiliti dalla Lega Serie A:.

Human replisomes direct a dedicated leading-strand primase for fork restart

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that DNA lesion bypass by leading-strand repriming was demonstrated for the core Escherichia coli replisome, in which primer synthesis is performed by the primase also responsible for lagging-strand replication12,13.
  • Industry observers note that unlike S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Disruptions to leading-strand synthesis impair and stall replication forks because DNA synthesis by the leading-strand polymerase, Pol ε, is essential for optimal template unwinding by the replicative CMG (CDC45–MCM–GINS) helicase1,2. Failure to efficiently restart and/or protect stalled replication forks is a major source of genomic instability3,4,5,6. Stalled forks can be restarted by a variety of mechanisms, including repriming downstream of the impediment4. In human cells, the primase–polymerase PRIMPOL promotes fork progression during replication stress7,8,9,10, but how its activity is coordinated by the replisome is unresolved. Here, by reconstituting replication fork stalling and restart with purified human proteins, we show that the CMG helicase directs PRIMPOL for efficient replication fork restart. Unexpectedly, the interaction between PRIMPOL and replication protein A9,11 is not critical for fork restart in this system. We show that PRIMPOL binds directly to CMG, and a cryo-electron microscopy structure illustrates how this targets PRIMPOL specifically for leading-strand priming to minimize the size of post-replicative gaps. Ablating the CMG–PRIMPOL interaction abolishes fork restart in vitro and PRIMPOL-dependent DNA damage tolerance in human cells. Our work establishes PRIMPOL as an integrated component of the human replisome dedicated to leading-strand priming.

Recent findings suggest that DNA lesion bypass by leading-strand repriming was demonstrated for the core Escherichia coli replisome, in which primer synthesis is performed by the primase also responsible for lagging-strand replication12,13. By contrast, eukaryotic replisomes reconstituted from purified Saccharomyces cerevisiae proteins cannot efficiently resume synthesis downstream of leading-strand lesions1 because the Pol α–primase complex that is responsible for priming each Okazaki fragment is targeted to the lagging-strand template14. This targeting mechanism is conserved in the human replisome14, indicating that inefficient priming on the leading strand by Pol α–primase is a universal feature of eukaryotic replisomes.

Industry observers note that unlike S. cerevisiae, humans have an additional primase called PRIMPOL7,8,9. PRIMPOL is a 560-amino-acid (aa) monomeric enzyme comprising a 21-aa amino-terminal helix of unknown function, an archaeo-eukaryotic primase (AEP) domain, a single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) binding zinc-finger (ZnF) and two C-terminal replication protein A (RPA) binding motifs (RBMs)6,15. Extensive evidence from human, mouse and chicken cell lines indicates that PRIMPOL promotes replication fork progression under conditions that stall replicative DNA polymerases8,9,10 and that this requires PRIMPOL primase activity10,16,17,18, leading to the formation of daughter-strand gaps5,19. Current models indicate that PRIMPOL is recruited to replication forks through a direct interaction with RPA9,11,16. However, because RPA is constitutively associated with the lagging-strand template, it is unclear whether this mode of recruitment is sufficient for efficient PRIMPOL priming on the leading strand, or whether an additional mechanism directs PRIMPOL specifically to the leading-strand template to rescue stalled replication forks.

Industry observers note that to investigate leading-strand repriming by PRIMPOL in the context of the replisome, we leveraged a system that we recently developed to assemble fast and efficient human replisomes from purified proteins20. In this approach, CMG is first loaded onto the forked end of a 9.7-kb DNA template before additional proteins are added to assemble replisomes that perform robust leading- and lagging-strand DNA replication (Fig. 1a). Pol ε performs the bulk of leading-strand synthesis, whereas Pol α–primase and Pol δ replicate the lagging strand. RFC and CTF18-RFC load the polymerase processivity factor PCNA onto the lagging and leading strands, respectively, and TIMELESS (TIM)–TIPIN, CLASPIN and AND1 associate with CMG to promote rapid replisome progression20. To monitor fork stalling and restart, a single cyclobutane pyrimidine dimer (CPD)—an important ultraviolet (UV)-induced DNA lesion and a potent block to replicative polymerases—was introduced to the leading-strand template 3.5 kb from the forked end1,20.

a, Schematic of the forked-DNA replication assay with a template containing a leading-strand CPD lesion. b, Time course of a replication assay on the leading-strand CPD template in the absence or presence of PRIMPOL. c, Two-dimensional gel analysis of a 30-min replication reaction in the presence of PRIMPOL.

Figure 1b shows that the CPD is a potent block to leading-strand DNA synthesis (3.5-kb stall lead product in denaturing gel), which causes replication forks to stall, as visualized by the slowly migrating species in the native gel (stalled fork). Similar replisome behaviour was observed when the CPD was substituted for a tetrahydrofuran abasic site (Extended Data Fig. 1a). Addition of PRIMPOL caused a reduction in the stalled fork population and the accumulation of full-length products in the native gel, concomitant with the appearance of an approximately 6.2-kb product in the denaturing gel (Fig. 1b, lanes 5–8, restart lead product). This result strongly indicated that PRIMPOL was promoting fork restart by leading-strand repriming. To confirm that the 6.2-kb products resulted from leading-strand repriming, products were analysed by two-dimensional gel electrophoresis (Fig. 1c). This showed that the 6.2-kb products were exclusively associated with the full-length product in the native gel and were roughly twice as intense as the 3.5-kb stall leading-strand product, as expected for bona fide restart products. Moreover, replication of the CPD template in the presence of a primase-defective PRIMPOL mutant (ZnFD2A)10 generated only stalled leading strands and Okazaki fragments (Extended Data Fig. 1b). These data illustrate the successful reconstitution of replication fork restart by leading-strand repriming using purified human proteins.

Replication fork restart also occurred efficiently after polymerase stalling at an abasic site (Extended Data Fig. 1c), suggesting that the mechanism of repriming is agnostic to the chemical nature of the initial blocking lesion. Restart also occurred independently of Pol δ (Extended Data Fig. 1d) and Pol α–primase (Extended Data Fig. 1c), illustrating that only Pol ε is required to extend the primer made by PRIMPOL in this system. Therefore, unless stated, Pol δ is omitted from subsequent experiments to avoid complications from strand-displacement synthesis.

Recent findings suggest that unlike Pol α–primase, which has a strong preference for rNTPs for primer synthesis21, following the 5′ rNTP, PRIMPOL incorporates dNTPs with a much higher efficiency than rNTPs owing to a sugar discrimination mechanism7,8,22. Consistent with these properties, omitting GTP, CTP and UTP did not compromise leading-strand restart (Extended Data Fig. 1e, compare lanes 7 and 8), indicating that ATP is sufficient for primer initiation in these assays. However, despite previous reports that manganese stimulates PRIMPOL priming activity in vitro8, its addition did not enhance the efficiency of restart (Extended Data Fig. 1f).

The observation that restart products were close to their maximum possible length (6.2 kb) indicated that they were initiated a very short distance from the lesion. To obtain a high-resolution view of leading-strand restart, we devised a strategy to map priming sites at near single-nucleotide resolution (Fig. 2a). To do so, products were post-replicatively digested with restriction enzymes that cut upstream and downstream of the lesion to liberate fragments that could be resolved in polyacrylamide sequencing gels. Figure 2b highlights that, apart from the stalled leading strand and a minor population of read-through products, a ladder of products was generated upon digestion of the PRIMPOL-containing reaction (lane 4). We conclude that each band in the ladder corresponds to a unique leading-strand repriming site. Notably, most of the PRIMPOL-dependent primers used to restart replication were synthesized within 50 nucleotides of the CPD, even when the PRIMPOL concentration was reduced to 5 nM (Extended Data Fig. 2a). An indistinguishable ladder pattern was observed following replication of the abasic site template (Extended Data Fig. 2b), showing that the chemical nature of the DNA lesion plays no part in priming site specification. Because CMG is likely to continue slowly unwinding DNA after polymerase stalling1,2, these data indicate that PRIMPOL activity is targeted to the leading-strand template immediately after polymerase stalling, which limits the size of the daughter-strand gap to generally <50 nucleotides on this template.

a, Schematic of the predicted products generated from digestion of replication products with SalI and NruI. b, Urea polyacrylamide gel of a 40-min replication reaction processed as in a. c, Schematic of the DNA template in which a 162-nt sequence after the CPD was replaced with an alternative sequence. d, Urea polyacrylamide gel of a 40-min replication reaction containing PRIMPOL, processed as in a. Pol δ was omitted from the experiments in b and d. Und, undamaged.

According to recent reports, previous work established that PRIMPOL exhibits sequence preferences for the initiation of primer synthesis23,24,25. We therefore reasoned that the distinct pattern of restart products in our experiments was a consequence of the DNA sequence downstream of the CPD. To test this, we modified a 162-nt region downstream of the CPD (Fig. 2c). Replication of this modified template in the presence of PRIMPOL generated a distinct pattern of restart products to those from the original CPD template (Fig. 2d, compare lanes 3 and 4). This demonstrates that leading-strand repriming by PRIMPOL in the context of the human replisome is modulated by DNA sequence. Importantly, despite the altered sequence, most restart products were again initiated within <50 nucleotides of the CPD, with one prominent product initiated about 100 nt from the CPD (Fig. 2d, lane 4). This is consistent with both templates containing multiple close matches to the preferred tri-nucleotide primer initiation sequence for PRIMPOL25.

The discovery that PRIMPOL-mediated repriming occurred a short distance from the CPD on two distinct templates suggested that an efficient mechanism directs PRIMPOL to the exposed leading-strand template. We hypothesized that this was mediated by the RBMs in the PRIMPOL C terminus11, recruiting PRIMPOL to RPA bound to the leading-strand template following polymerase stalling at the CPD and continued template unwinding by CMG. To examine this, we generated two PRIMPOL mutants defective in RPA binding: one lacking both RBMs and the other carrying a mutant in RBM-A (RBM-ARA) that abolished PRIMPOL localization to chromatin in human cells11 (Fig. 3a). Figure 3b shows that both PRIMPOL mutants promoted leading-strand restart with comparable efficiency to wild-type PRIMPOL. Moreover, analysis of restart products revealed that both mutants exhibited the same repriming site pattern as wild-type PRIMPOL (Fig. 3c). We conclude that RBM-mediated interactions between PRIMPOL and RPA are non-essential for replication fork restart with reconstituted human replisomes.

Sources indicate that a, Primary structure diagrams showing full-length PRIMPOL and PRIMPOL point mutants and truncations. b, Denaturing agarose gel analysis of a 40-min replication reaction with the indicated PRIMPOL mutants. c, Urea polyacrylamide gel analysis of a 40-min replication reaction on the CPD template performed with the indicated PRIMPOL RPA binding mutants. Products were digested post-replicatively with SalI and NruI. d, Denaturing agarose gel analysis of a 40-min replication reaction with dropouts of non-essential replisome components on undamaged and CPD templates in the presence of PRIMPOL. e, Silver-stained SDS–PAGE analysis of a pull-down experiment with the indicated proteins. WT, wild type.

The non-essentiality of the PRIMPOL RBMs for fork restart, together with the very close proximity of repriming to the lesion, prompted us to explore the idea that PRIMPOL might be directed to stalled forks through an interaction with the core replisome. Omission of all non-essential core replisome components individually did not abolish leading-strand restart (Fig. 3d). We therefore hypothesized that PRIMPOL might be recruited directly by the CMG helicase. Consistent with this idea, the pull-down experiment in Fig. 3e shows that PRIMPOL interacts specifically with CMG.

To investigate how PRIMPOL is recruited to CMG, and how this might facilitate efficient leading-strand repriming, we determined a structure of PRIMPOL bound to CMG by single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) (Extended Data Fig. 3a–d and Extended Data Table 1). Well-resolved cryo-EM density was recovered for the PRIMPOL AEP domain alongside the ATPase domains of MCM4 and MCM7 that form part of the C-terminal tier (C-tier) of the two-tiered hexameric MCM ring (Fig. 4a,b). This arrangement is mediated by a conserved 21-aa α-helix at the N terminus of PRIMPOL binding to MCM7 and an approximately 20-aa loop immediately downstream of the helix that is sandwiched between a shallow groove on MCM4 and the PRIMPOL AEP domain (Fig. 4b,c and Extended Data Fig. 4a,b). The PRIMPOL AEP domain is positioned laterally adjacent to the exit of the MCM central pore, through which the unwound leading-strand template emerges. Moreover, superimposing the crystal structure of PRIMPOL bound to primer-template DNA26 onto the AEP domain in our structure shows that its catalytic core is oriented to support primer synthesis directly as template DNA is fed from CMG (Fig. 4d and Extended Data Fig. 4c).

a, Cryo-EM density map of the CMG–PRIMPOL structure coloured by subunit occupancy. b, Close-up view of PRIMPOL bound to MCM4 and MCM7. The atomic model is shown in ribbon representation; the cryo-EM density is shown as a semi-transparent surface. c, Primary structure diagram of PRIMPOL with the regions visible in the cryo-EM structure shown in pink. d, Model illustrating the possible path of DNA from CMG to PRIMPOL. The protein structure shown is the CMG–PRIMPOL structure from this study. The DNA in the model was generated by superpositioning the PRIMPOL–DNA structure (Protein Data Bank (PDB): 5L2X) and CMG-forked DNA structure (PDB: 7PFO) onto the PRIMPOL–CMG structure in this study.

Guided by our cryo-EM structure, to evaluate the role of the CMG–PRIMPOL interaction in replication fork restart, we removed the first 39 aa of PRIMPOL (PRIMPOL∆1–39) (Fig. 5a and Extended Data Fig. 5a). Figure 5b shows that wild-type PRIMPOL but not PRIMPOL∆1–39 was robustly pulled down by CMG, confirming that the PRIMPOL N terminus harbours the primary CMG interaction motifs. PRIMPOL∆1–39 retained primase activity on a ssDNA template (Extended Data Fig. 5b) but was unable to promote fork restart by leading-strand repriming in the human replisome (Fig. 5c,d, lane 4). This defect was not rescued by Pol δ addition (Extended Data Fig. 5c). We conclude that the interaction between PRIMPOL and CMG is essential for leading-strand repriming by reconstituted human replisomes.

Mutants generated within that region are shown. b, Silver-stained and western blot SDS–PAGE analysis of a pull-down experiment with the indicated proteins. c,d, Denaturing agarose (c) and urea polyacrylamide (d) gel analysis of 40-min replication reactions with PRIMPOL mutants. Samples in d were digested post-replicatively with SalI and NruI. e, Close-up view of the interaction between PRIMPOL and MCM4. The model is shown in ribbon representation in semi-transparent cryo-EM density. Amino acid residues targeted for mutagenesis are depicted (sticks). f, Denaturing agarose gel analysis of a 40-min replication reaction on the CPD template with the indicated PRIMPOL concentrations. g, Cisplatin sensitivity assay performed for the TK6 cell lines specified. The data are the average of three biological replicates, and error bars represent the standard deviation. P values are the result of statistical testing using two-way analysis of cell survival data by fitting a linear quadratic model with maximum likelihood (see Extended Data Table 2 for all P values); pcnaK164R compared with +PRIMPOL∆1–39 P** = 0.0064554, primpol/pcnaK164R compared with +PRIMPOL P* = 0.024598.

We next investigated whether the interaction between PRIMPOL and CMG functions exclusively in PRIMPOL recruitment or whether accurate positioning of the AEP domain is necessary for efficient replication fork restart. Abolishing PRIMPOL interaction with MCM7 by removing the α-helix at the extreme N terminus of PRIMPOL (Fig. 5a, PRIMPOL∆1–21) resulted in a modest reduction in leading-strand restart (Fig. 5c, denaturing, lane 5), with a disproportionate effect on initiation events that occurred closest to the CPD (Fig. 5d, Urea PAGE, lane 5). Retaining α-helix 1–21 but substituting the ensuing loop (aa 22–39) with a glycine–serine linker (Fig. 5a, PRIMPOLGS22–39), or substituting six residues in the loop to alanine (Fig. 5a, PRIMPOL6A loop), resulted in complete loss of restart products (Fig. 5c,d, lanes 6 and 7). These results highlight the importance of this loop, which sits between MCM4 and the PRIMPOL AEP domain, for leading-strand restart.

It has been revealed that furthermore, targeting three loop residues that sit at the interface with MCM4 (Arg31, Leu32 and Ser33; Fig. 5a, PRIMPOL3A loop) resulted in a less severe defect than a mutant targeting the side chains of Tyr28 and Arg29 to disrupt the bridging interaction between MCM4 and the PRIMPOL AEP domain (Fig. 5a, PRIMPOL2A loop) (Fig. 5c–e). This observation strongly suggests that rigid PRIMPOL positioning alongside the MCM C-tier is necessary for efficient leading-strand restart in the human replisome.

In our reconstituted system, the interaction between PRIMPOL and CMG (Fig. 5c), but not between PRIMPOL RBMs and RPA (Fig. 3b), is essential for fork restart. Therefore, because PRIMPOL RBM-A is required for PRIMPOL activity in cells9,11,16,17, we hypothesized that the RBM-mediated interaction might serve to increase the local concentration of PRIMPOL at the replication fork. This function may not be required under our standard in vitro reaction conditions, which use a relatively high concentration (20 nM) of PRIMPOL. To test this idea, we performed a titration of wild-type PRIMPOL and PRIMPOLΔRBM. With wild-type PRIMPOL, leading-strand restart became less efficient only when the protein concentration was reduced to 0.1 nM (Fig. 5f and Extended Data Fig. 5d). By contrast, leading-strand restart was compromised at 1 nM PRIMPOLΔRBM and was barely detectable at 0.1 nM. These findings are consistent with a model in which the RBM-mediated interaction between PRIMPOL and RPA facilitates PRIMPOL localization at the replication fork.

Loss of PRIMPOL does not sensitize many human cell lines to DNA damage because of redundant DNA damage tolerance pathways27,28,29. Therefore, to evaluate whether the interaction between PRIMPOL and CMG is required for PRIMPOL function in human cells, we took advantage of our recent finding that loss of PRIMPOL sensitizes translesion synthesis (TLS)-deficient TK6 lymphoblastoid cells to cisplatin, most prominently observed in cells unable to ubiquitinate PCNA at lysine 164 (ref. 27). PRIMPOL was removed by CRISPR–Cas9 targeting in pcnaK164R cells. Figure 5g indicates that loss of PRIMPOL further sensitized pcnaK164R cells to cisplatin, consistent with our previous work27. Whereas expression of wild-type PRIMPOL fully rescued this phenotype, expression of PRIMPOL∆1–39 did not complement the additional cisplatin sensitivity of pcnaK164R cells (Fig. 5g, Extended Data Fig. 6 and Extended Data Table 2). These data indicate that the interaction between CMG and PRIMPOL, which is essential for fork restart in vitro, is notable for PRIMPOL-mediated DNA damage tolerance in human cells.

On the basis of our results and previous work, we propose the following model for replication fork restart by PRIMPOL-dependent repriming (Fig. 6a). Our biochemical reconstitution has demonstrated that the PRIMPOL RBMs are not essential for leading-strand repriming in vitro. However, they do become vital for fork restart at low PRIMPOL concentrations, and evidence from cellular studies indicates that RBM-A is required for PRIMPOL recruitment to chromatin and fork progression during replication stress9,11,16,17. To accommodate these observations, we propose that the interaction of PRIMPOL with RPA, which is low affinity11 and therefore likely to be transient, serves primarily to localize PRIMPOL to actively replicating genomic loci, which may be necessary because PRIMPOL is a relatively low abundance protein in human cells15,30 (Fig. 6a).

It has been revealed that a, Model for CMG-directed replication fork restart by PRIMPOL after the replisome encounters a leading-strand DNA lesion (red triangle). Two non-mutually exclusive mechanisms are shown. In (i), PRIMPOL is recruited to CMG only after fork stalling at the lesion. In (ii), PRIMPOL can associate with CMG and travel with the replisome before fork stalling. b, Composite model of the human replisome showing the positions of PRIMPOL, Pol ε and Pol α–primase. The model is a composite of the following PDB files: 8B9D, 7PFO and 9F6D. The position of the Pol ε catalytic domain (9F6D) is based on a yeast replisome structure42.

According to recent reports, on encountering a DNA lesion, leading-strand synthesis by Pol ε is blocked, but CMG continues to translocate along the template at a greatly reduced rate1,2, exposing ssDNA on the leading-strand template between the helicase and polymerase (Fig. 6a). Through its interactions with MCM4 and MCM7, PRIMPOL is positioned to capture the exposed ssDNA to initiate leading-strand repriming (Fig. 6a, pathway (i)). After primer synthesis, Pol ε must reengage the leading strand for optimal fork progression to resume. The anchoring of PRIMPOL on CMG suggests a pathway in which the primer might be handed off directly to the leading-strand PCNA loader CTF18-RFC and then to Pol ε. Alternatively, Pol δ might facilitate the recoupling of leading-strand synthesis by extending the primer made by PRIMPOL until it reaches CMG, at which point the 3′ end is transferred to Pol ε. This pathway has been observed following leading-strand lesion bypass by TLS in the yeast replisome31.

The direct interaction of PRIMPOL with CMG raises the possibility that PRIMPOL could travel with CMG to facilitate its immediate deployment on helicase–polymerase uncoupling (Fig. 6a, pathway (ii)). In this regard, it is noteworthy that PRIMPOL does not clash with any known core replisome protein, including Pol ε (Fig. 6b). However, because the MCM4 and MCM7 ATPase domains undergo conformational changes during CMG translocation that could affect PRIMPOL binding, single-molecule studies will be required to determine if PRIMPOL can stably associate with moving replisomes.

In a recent development, the mechanism of PRIMPOL recruitment via MCM4 and MCM7 ensures that repriming is tightly coupled to CMG progression to limit the size of the ssDNA gap that is left for post-replicative repair pathways. Our work further establishes that PRIMPOL displays a sequence preference for primer synthesis. Based on prior studies, this sequence is short and somewhat degenerate25, which should enable efficient repriming at most genomic loci. However, regions of the genome devoid of optimal priming sites are likely to exist, for example in repetitive DNA, which could limit repriming and bias fork restart and stabilisation towards alternative pathways.

According to recent reports, the two-stage model for PRIMPOL recruitment involving both RPA and CMG interactions is analogous to a mechanism proposed for the recruitment of TLS polymerases to the replication fork32. This mechanism has been observed in the E. coli replisome for the TLS polymerase PolIV, where an interaction with the single-stranded DNA-binding protein SSB concentrates PolIV at the fork to promote its interaction with the sliding clamp β33. We also note that RPA will accumulate on the leading-strand template during prolonged uncoupling, which should enhance PRIMPOL recruitment to stressed replication forks.

Industry observers note that apart from its low abundance, PRIMPOL activity is regulated by checkpoint and cell cycle kinases6,34,35,36, suggesting that excessive repriming and daughter-strand gap formation is deleterious. Tight regulation of PRIMPOL might also indicate a capacity of the enzyme to interfere with normal replisome function. We reasoned that this could be a consequence of PRIMPOL being directed to the leading strand by CMG, causing it to interfere with Pol ε by competing for the nascent leading strand. Consistent with this idea, addition of PRIMPOL mildly slowed fork progression on an undamaged template, and this effect was exacerbated by omission of CTF18-RFC, which compromises PCNA loading on the leading strand (Extended Data Fig. 7a). Importantly, this inhibition was dependent on the interaction of PRIMPOL with CMG but not on primase activity (Extended Data Fig. 7b).

According to recent reports, the widespread phylogenetic distribution of PRIMPOL37, and the conservation of its CMG interaction motifs, indicates an evolutionary pressure to keep replication forks moving by repriming. It also indicates that in the absence of chronic replication stress, repriming might be the default response of the replisome to impediments to leading-strand synthesis. This raises the possibility that leading-strand synthesis might be considerably more discontinuous in human cells than previously appreciated. It is also interesting to consider that PRIMPOL could access the leading strand for priming potentially in any instance where synthesis is paused, for example during PCNA loading on the leading strand by CTF18-RFC. This is possibly a frequent occurrence because PCNA abundance is reported to be similar on leading and lagging strands in yeast38.

Multiple pathways collaborate to protect and restart stalled replication forks during replication stress. Ablating replication fork reversal factors has been found to promote fork progression in a PRIMPOL-dependent manner6,34,39,40,41, suggesting an interplay between repriming and replication fork remodelling. The factors that dictate the balance between repriming and other fork processing pathways (for example, fork reversal), and how this is influenced by the CMG–PRIMPOL interaction, is an crucial area for future study, especially given that PRIMPOL promotes chemoresistance in BRCA1 deficient cells34.

It has been revealed that for decades, prokaryotic and eukaryotic replisomes were thought to function with a single primase to initiate DNA synthesis on both template strands. This changed with the discovery of PRIMPOL as a second primase in many eukaryotic species, including humans7,8,9. However, although it has been demonstrated that PRIMPOL facilitates replication fork progression during replication stress in a range of metazoan cell lines, evidence for PRIMPOL primase activity being directed specifically to the leading-strand template, and a plausible mechanism for this targeting, was lacking. The work presented here demonstrates that, through its interactions with CMG, PRIMPOL is a dedicated leading-strand primase, establishing a division of labour in the human replisome: Pol α–primase acts on the lagging strand14, while PRIMPOL operates on the leading strand. Our data, together with the strong conservation of CMG-binding motifs in the PRIMPOL N terminus, indicate that many eukaryotic replisomes rely on strand-specific primases to maintain efficient replisome progression, and that this specificity is governed by helicase-directed primase recruitment to the replication fork.

Replication reactions were performed essentially as described previously, with the following modifications. Reactions were assembled stepwise: DNA (2.4 nM) was first incubated with CMG (50 nM) for 10 min in replication buffer supplemented with 0.1 mM AMP-PNP. Following this pre-incubation, the mixture was diluted two-fold with replication buffer containing 30 μM dATP and dCTP. Additional replication factors (20 nM PCNA, 20 nM RFC, 20 nM Pol ε, 10 nM Pol α, 20 nM CLASPIN, 20 nM TIM–TIPIN, 20 nM AND1 and 20 nM CTF18-RFC) were included at this stage unless stated otherwise. Replication was initiated by adding a concentrated start mix supplying 4 mM ATP; 30 µM dTTP and dGTP; 200 µM GTP, CTP and UTP; 33 nM α-[32P]-dCTP; and 100 nM RPA. When present, 20 nM PRIMPOL was added 2–3 min after replication had started. For reactions containing Pol δ, potassium glutamate was increased to 250 mM, and the polymerase was added at 2 nM immediately before the start mix. Leading-strand restart reactions were typically incubated for 20–40 min and terminated with EDTA to 50 mM. Unincorporated radiolabel was removed using Illustra MicroSpin G-50 columns. Replication products were separated by alkaline agarose electrophoresis (0.7% agarose, 30 mM NaOH, 2 mM EDTA) run for 16.5 h at 24 V, fixed in cold 5% trichloroacetic acid, dried on Whatman paper, and visualized using an Amersham Typhoon phosphorimager scanner.

For analysis under native conditions, terminated reactions were supplemented with SDS (0.1%) and proteinase K (0.2 mg ml−1; New England Biolabs) and incubated for 10 min at 37 °C. DNA was purified by phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol extraction (25:24:1; TE-equilibrated) and passed through Illustra MicroSpin G-50 columns to remove unincorporated nucleotides. Samples were then digested with SapI–PciI for 30 min at 37 °C to remove the template ends and prevent end-labelled species in gels. Following digestion, reactions underwent a second SDS/proteinase K treatment and phenol:chloroform extraction to ensure complete protein removal. DNA was ethanol-precipitated, washed with 70% ethanol, resuspended in native loading dye (20 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0, 50 mM EDTA, 10% Ficoll 400, 2% N-lauroylsarcosine sodium salt solution), and resolved on 1% agarose gels run overnight at 24 V in modified 1× TAE buffer (50 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.9, 40 mM sodium acetate, 1 mM EDTA pH 8.0). Gels were dried and imaged as described above.

For two-dimensional (2D) gel analysis, samples were prepared as for native conditions and loaded into two lanes of a native agarose gel, with 10% of the reaction applied to one lane and the remaining 90% to the other. After electrophoresis, the lane containing the bulk of the sample was excised and placed horizontally along the top of a 0.7% denaturing agarose gel for the second dimension, which was run for 16.5 h at 27 V. Gels were then processed and imaged as described for alkaline gels.

In a recent development, for analysis on denaturing polyacrylamide gels, samples were prepared as for native conditions, but digested with SalI–NruI instead, and resuspended in loading dye (95% formamide, 20 mM EDTA, 0.04% Bromophenol Blue and 0.04% xylene cyanol). Samples were boiled for 5 min at 75 °C and resolved on a 40 cm × 20 cm 3.5% denaturing polyacrylamide gel. Gels were run in 1× TBE for 150 min at 40 W and dried as described above.

DNA substrates were prepared following previously published methods1,20. Gapped pZN3 was produced by introducing two adjacent Nt.BbvCI nicks and heating the plasmid to release the short intervening oligonucleotide, which was subsequently displaced using a sequestering oligonucleotide. The resulting gapped plasmid was purified on a Sepharose 4B (Sigma-Aldrich 4B200) gel filtration column. A 10-fold molar excess of a short oligonucleotide containing a CPD lesion, an abasic site or an undamaged control sequence (listed in Supplementary Table 1) was then annealed into the gap and ligated to generate the damaged or control templates. Finally, the DNA was digested with SapI, ligated to a pre-annealed fork structure, and purified again over a Sepharose 4B column.

Industry observers note that replication proteins were expressed in either E. coli or insect cells (Sf9 and Hi-5) and were purified following the methods described previously20,43. For more details about the purification steps, see Supplementary Table 2.

Relevant plasmids for protein expression were transformed into Rosetta2 cells using standard bacterial transformation protocols. A single transformant colony was selected and cultured in 1 l LB media supplemented with 50 µg ml−1 kanamycin and 10 µg ml−1 chloramphenicol overnight at 30 °C without agitation. The following morning, the culture temperature was increased to 37 °C and incubated with shaking at 210 rpm. On reaching an optical density (OD600) of 0.6–0.8, protein expression was induced by the addition of 1 mM IPTG for 3 h. Cells were subsequently harvested, washed with PBS and flash-frozen for storage.

In a recent development, wild-type and mutant PRIMPOL proteins were purified using the following protocol. Cell pellets were resuspended in lysis buffer containing 50 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.0), 1 M NaCl, 10% glycerol, 0.1% Triton X-100, 0.5 mM TCEP and protease inhibitors (cOmplete, EDTA-free; Roche). The cells were lysed by sonication (three cycles of 1 min each, consisting of 5 s ‘on’ and 5 s ‘off’ pulses at 40% amplitude), and insoluble material was removed by centrifugation at 235,000g for 50 min at 4 °C. The clarified lysate was incubated with 1 ml Strep-Tactin XT Superflow high-capacity resin for 1 h at 4 °C. The resin was then collected and washed extensively with 100 ml lysis buffer, followed by sequential washes with 25 ml lysis buffer containing 0.55 M NaCl and 35 ml lysis buffer containing 0.1 M NaCl to reduce the salt concentration. Bound protein was eluted in 1 ml fractions using eight column volumes of 0.1 M NaCl lysis buffer supplemented with 30 mM biotin. Protein-containing fractions were pooled and loaded onto a 5 ml HiTrap Heparin HP column pre-equilibrated in 0.1 M NaCl buffer. The protein was eluted with a 20 column volume linear gradient from 100 mM to 1 M NaCl. Peak fractions were pooled and dialysed overnight against 1 l of storage buffer containing 25 mM HEPES-KOH (pH 7.6), 0.3 M potassium acetate, 10% glycerol, 0.02% NP-40-S and 0.5 mM TCEP. Finally, the protein was concentrated using a 30 kDa molecular weight cut-off spin concentrator (Amicon Ultra-30), flash-frozen in liquid nitrogen and stored at −80 °C.

Reactions (20 µl) were performed in buffer containing 25 mM HEPES-KOH pH 7.6, 150 mM potassium glutamate, 10 mM magnesium acetate, 0.05% NP-40, and 1 mM DTT. CMG (5 pmol) was incubated with PRIMPOL (10 pmol; wild-type or Δ1–39) for 30 min on ice. A 2 µl aliquot was removed as input, and the remaining mixture was incubated with 5 µl α-Flag magnetic beads equilibrated in buffer for 30 min at 4 °C with shaking (1,250 rpm). Beads were washed three times with 100 µl reaction buffer, and bound proteins were eluted for 30 min at 4 °C at 1,250 rpm in 20 µl buffer containing 0.2 mg ml−1 Flag peptide. Eluates were mixed with loading buffer and analysed by 4–12% SDS–PAGE alongside input samples, followed by silver staining and western blotting.

Protein samples from pull-down assays with purified proteins were resolved on NuPAGE Novex 4–12% Bis-Tris gels (Thermo Fisher) in MOPS buffer and transferred to PVDF membranes using the iBlot Dry Transfer System (Life Technologies). Membranes were blocked for 30 min at room temperature in 5% milk-TBST. For the detection of PRIMPOL, membranes were incubated for 1 h at room temperature with anti-PRIMPOL (Proteintech; 29824-1-AP, see Supplementary Table 3) followed by a secondary antibody incubation for another hour at room temperature (anti-rabbit-HRP, see Supplementary Table 3). For the detection of strep-SLD5, membranes were incubated for 2 h at room temperature with anti-strep-HRP antibody. Both membranes were subsequently incubated with Amersham ECL western blotting detection reagent, and the emitted chemiluminescence was detected on film and developed in an automatic film processor. The films were scanned using an Epson Scan V850 pro.

For the detection of PRIMPOL from TK6 extracts, protein was extracted from cells by lysing cells directly with RIPA buffer (Thermo Fisher) supplemented with 1× protease inhibitor cocktail (Sigma) for 10 min on ice. To quantify protein concentration, a BCA assay was performed using the Pierce Protein Assay Kit (Thermo) as per kit instructions. Protein lysate (20 µg) was prepared with 1× Laemmli sample buffer (Bio-Rad), supplemented with 10% β-mercaptoethanol. Denatured protein was run using NuPAGE Novex 4–12% Bis-Tris gels (Thermo Fisher). The samples were then transferred onto a PVDF membrane. The membranes were blocked in 5% BSA in Tris-buffered saline (TBS) with 1% Tween (TBS-T) for 2 h at room temperature with rocking. The blocked membranes were incubated in blocking buffer with primary antibodies (Supplementary Table 3) at 4 °C for 12–20 h. Membranes were incubated with Licor IRDye 800CW Rabbit secondary antibody at 20,000× dilution in blocking buffer for 30 min at room temperature. Membranes were washed three times with 10 ml fresh TBS-T for 5 min at room temperature with rocking. Antibody detection and image capture were carried out using the Bio-Rad ChemiDoc.

Industry observers note that reactions were adapted from a previously described study11. Human RPA (240 nM) was first incubated with 5 nM M13 single-stranded DNA (Fresh England Biolabs) for 10 min at 37 °C in 10 µl reactions containing 25 mM HEPES-KOH (pH 7.6), 100 mM potassium acetate, 10 mM magnesium acetate, 0.01% NP-40, 1 mM DTT, 0.1 mg ml−1 BSA, 400 µM rNTPs, 80 µM dNTPs, 3 mM ATP and 33 nM α-[32P]-dCTP. PRIMPOL (400 nM; wild-type or mutants) was then added, and reactions were incubated for a further 30 min at 37 °C. DNA synthesis was stopped with 50 mM EDTA, and unincorporated radiolabel was removed using illustra MicroSpin G-50 columns. The samples were mixed with loading buffer (95% formamide, 20 mM EDTA, 0.04% Bromophenol Blue and 0.04% xylene cyanol), heated at 75 °C for 5 min, and resolved on a 40 cm × 20 cm 10% denaturing polyacrylamide gel run at 40 W for 105 min. The gels were dried and imaged as described above.

PRIMPOL, purified as described above, was concentrated using an Amicon Ultra centrifugal filter with a 30 kDa MWCO and injected onto a 2.4 ml S200 increase 3.2/300 column equilibrated with 40 mM HEPES-KOH pH 7.6, 80 mM KOAc, 1 mM DTT. The peak fractions were collected and adjusted with buffer to a concentration of 5.7 µM. CMG was dialysed overnight against 40 mM HEPES-KOH pH 7.6, 80 mM KOAc, 1 mM DTT, mixed with 1.3-fold molar excess of PRIMPOL, supplemented with 3.3 mM ATP and incubated on ice for at least 20 min before cryo-EM grid preparation. After incubation on ice, 2 µl of the sample was applied to freshly glow-discharged (Edwards Sputter Coater S150B, 45 s at 30 mA) UltrAuFoil R1.2/1.3, manually blotted on the top face for 2 s and immediately plunged into liquid ethane at liquid nitrogen temperature. Two datasets of 8,160 and 8,103 raw movies, respectively, were acquired using a 300 kV TFS Titan Krios microscope equipped with a Falcon 4i direct electron detector operated in electron counting mode using ThermoFisher EPU with AFIS enabled. The movies were collected over a defocus range of −1.0 µm to −2.6 µm, at an effective pixel size of 0.84 Å per pixel.

The data processing pipeline is shown as a schematic in Extended Data Fig. 4a. Raw movies were motion-corrected and dose-weighted using the implementation of a MotionCor2-like program of RELION44,45 (Extended Data Table 1) and then imported to CryoSPARC v.4.7.1 (ref. 46) for further processing. For each dataset, the particles were first ‘blob’-picked and extracted with 4-fold binning (336 Å box size). The 2D classification was run on a subset of 50,000 particles, and classes showing features for CMG in 2D-class averages were selected. Ab initio reconstruction was performed with the selected particles and, separately, with the remaining particles to generate three-dimensional (3D) volumes for either CMG or ‘noise/junk’-classes. The obtained volumes were provided as 3D references in two iterative rounds of heterogeneous refinement of all extracted particles, the first round of which the particles of the best class were selected for the second round. Independently, 2D class averages were used for template-based picking, and the resulting particles were also subjected to two iterative rounds of heterogeneous refinement as described above. The particles of the best 3D class from each picking strategy were combined and duplicate particles were removed. The resulting particles were used for homogeneous refinement with minimization over per-particle scale enabled, after which the particle population with poor signal (relative per-particle scale below 0.75) was removed. The remaining particles were subjected to 3D classification using a focus mask around the C-tier of the MCM ring, and particle classes with good definition for secondary structure features in the MCM C-tier were selected. At this stage, particles from datasets 1 and 2 were combined and locally refined using a focus mask around the AAA+ ATPase domains of MCM4 and MCM7. The resulting 3D reconstruction displayed density for the AEP domain of PRIMPOL around which a local mask was drawn for 3D classification. The largest class (135,661 particles) also exhibited the strongest signal for PRIMPOL. The particles were recentred on a mask around PRIMPOL and ATPase domains of MCM4 and MCM7, re-extracted (280-pixel box, downsampled to 160 pixels, 1.47 Å per pixel) and subjected to signal subtraction with an inverted mask around PRIMPOL and ATPase domains of MCM4 and MCM7. The subtracted particles were used for 3D classification from which the classes with the best density for the PRIMPOL AEP domain were selected (65,500 particles). The 30,000-particle subset with the best per-particle scale was then used for 3DFlex47 to reconstruct the final map for the PRIMPOL AEP domain near the AAA+ ATPase domains of MCM4 and MCM7 (map 1, 3.5 Å resolution). The same particle subset was reverted to the original (non-subtracted) images, re-extracted from the original micrographs without binning (440-pixel box, 0.84 Å per pixel) using particle poses from global refinement on the CMG helicase. The obtained particles were subjected to homogeneous refinement to reconstruct a consensus map (map 2), or to local refinements with either a focus mask on CMG components GINS, CDC45 and the N-tier of the MCM ring (map 3, 3.1 Å resolution), or a focus mask on the C-tier of the MCM ring (map 4, 3.3 Å resolution). Maps coloured by estimated local resolution are shown in Extended Data Fig. 4c. Fourier shell correlation plots are shown in Extended Data Fig. 4d. Focus maps (maps 1, 3 and 4) were fitted into the consensus volume (map 2) using ChimeraX48. An initial atomic model was obtained by rigid-body fitting previously reported structures of CMG (6XTX, 7PFO) and PRIMPOL (5L2X) into the consensus EM volume using ChimeraX26,43,49. The fit-to-density was subsequently refined using ISOLDE50 inside ChimeraX. ATP–ADP ligands and gaps in the model were built de novo in Coot51. The molecular model was then used together with the consensus map and all focus maps to generate a composite EM map using phenix.combine_focused_maps by Thomas Terwilliger. Model geometry and atomic displacement parameters were refined against the composite map using phenix.real_space_refine52, after which model validation was carried out using MolProbity53 inside Phenix. Statistics for cryo-EM data acquisition, processing and molecular model refinement are summarized in Extended Data Table 1. Root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) between PRIMPOL–CMG (this study) and PRIMPOL–DNA (5L2X) was calculated in PyMOL (www.pymol.org) for 1,987 pairs of common atoms (RMSD = 1.723) or 253 pairs of common Cα atoms (RMSD = 1.374).

Recent findings suggest that all TK6 cell lines were cultured in RPMI 1640 medium with GlutaMAX (Gibco) supplemented with 10% FBS (Gibco). The cells were grown at 37 °C and 5% CO2. The cells were maintained between 0.05 cells ml −1 and 1.0 × 106 cells ml−1.

For the generation of plasmids for protein purification, plasmid MT_FB (see Supplementary Table 4 for details) was used as a template to generate the rest of PRIMPOL mutants in this study.

Sources indicate that for the generation of plasmids for cellular studies, the m6p-PRIMPOL-WT_GFP_BSD plasmid backbone (wild-type PRIMPOL with GFP tag) (Supplementary Table 4) was used to generate the PRIMPOL ∆1–39 mutant (truncation mutant with GFP co-expression), using the Q5 Site-Directed Mutagenesis Kit (NEB) as per kit instructions. See Supplementary Table 1 for primers used.

In a recent development, TK6 primpol/pcnaK164R cells were used for expression of mutant and wild-type PRIMPOL–GFP. PRIMPOL Δ1–39 and wild-type PRIMPOL were expressed through plasmids that contained resistance cassettes for blasticidin. Plasmid DNA (15 µg) was electroporated into 20 × 106 cells using the Neon electroporator (Thermo Fisher) with the following conditions: 100 µl Resuspension Buffer R, 1,400 V and 20 ms. The electroporated cells were seeded across 96-well plates in growth media containing 7.5 µg ml−1 blasticidin. The surviving colonies were expanded and subjected to single-cell sorting for positive GFP expression through FACS to generate clonal populations.

Recent findings suggest that viscous culture medium (5 ml) consisting of 11.9 g l−1 RPMI 1640 powder with l-glutamine supplement (Gibco), 2 g l−1 sodium hydrogen carbonate (Sigma-Aldrich), 10 g l−1 4,000 cP methylcellulose (Thermo Fisher), 100 U l−1 penicillin/streptomycin (Gibco) and 1× GlutaMAX supplement (Gibco) was added to wells of six-well plates. The plates were equilibrated at 37 °C, 10% CO2 for a minimum of 1 h. The cells were treated with the indicated dose of cisplatin for 1 h at 37 °C and 10% CO2. The cells were then pelleted at 1,200 rpm for 5 min and resuspended in fresh growth media to stop the cisplatin treatment. Then, 500,000, 50,000 or 5,000 cells were added to duplicate wells of the six-well plates for each cell line or condition. The plates were incubated at 37 °C, 5% CO2 until well-defined colonies were visible.

In a recent development, flow cytometry was used to confirm the expression of GFP in TK6 primpol/pcnaK164R cell lines. A total of 1 × 106 cells were pelleted at 1,200 rpm for 5 min and resuspended in 1 ml PBS supplemented with 2% FBS. The cells were analysed by flow cytometry using a Becton Dickinson LSRFortessa. TK6 primpol and TK6 wild-type cells were used as negative controls for GFP expression. Cell sorting of GFP-positive cells was performed using a Becton Dickinson FACSAria Fusion, with cells sorted into single cells per well of a 96-well plate. Flow cytometry data were plotted using FlowJo.

Recent findings suggest that for the colony survival assay in TK6 human cells in Fig. 5g, individual colonies in each well were counted using a custom macro-script in ImageJ, and the percentage survival relative to untreated cells was calculated to assess clonogenic survival. Statistical testing was performed by the R package CFAssay using two-way analysis of the cell survival data by fitting a linear quadratic model with maximum likelihood (Extended Data Table 2).

Experiments in Figs. 1c, 3d and 5b and Extended Data Figs. 1a,c–e, 2b, 3b, 5c and 7a,b were performed twice. Colony survival assay in TK6 human cells (Fig. 5g) was performed three times, testing two independent clones of primpol/pcnaK164R + PRIMPOLΔ1–39. Cryo-EM sample preparation was performed twice.

Recent findings suggest that in vista della gara di questo pomeriggio (ore 18:45) contro il Real Madrid in Women’s Champions League, la centrale difensiva dell’Inter Ivana Andres ha parlato ai canali ufficiali dell’Inter. Per lei infatti si tratta di una gara molto sentita visto che ha vestito la maglia del club spagnolo dal 2020 al 2024 collezionando 137 presenze.

“Servirà restare molto concentrate e fare il nostro gioco in questa partita, questo è quello che ci chiede il mister. Dobbiamo avere la massima attenzione nel corso dei 90 minuti e mantenere l’ambizione di conquistare i tre punti. - spiega la classe ‘94 a Inter TV – Tornare a Madrid per me è speciale, è stata casa mia per quattro anni e penso che sarà una partita emozionante avendo tanti ricordi”.

Recent findings suggest that la centrale poi si concentra sul suo reparto: “La difesa è il miglior attacco, se non subisci gol sei sicura di non poter perdere la partita. Difendere e attaccare bene però è una responsabilità che riguarda tutta la squadra. A livello personale io cerco sempre di dare il massimo per le mie compagne e per la squadra".

Industry observers note that bruno Guimarães cupped his ears and had a plastic cup thrown at him as the abuse came down from the stands. Despite the missiles, the Brazilian wore a look that made it clear he was very much enjoying his first goal in an Arsenal shirt.

It has been revealed that mikel Arteta has laid bare his quirky management techniques so his players are ready for any eventuality. Late meals and making the dressing room hotter are among his tricks, although nothing can prepare a player having 40,000 fans calling you a “sad Geordie b------”.

So it was a sweet moment for Guimarães, even more so after coming just after Sunderland had a penalty saved. Just 121 seconds after Enzo Le Fée had his spot kick tipped on to a post by David Raya, Guimarães was rubbing salt into the wound with a stunning long-range strike that went in off the crossbar.

Sources indicate that the former Newcastle captain gave the perfect response after being taunted his old rivals. “It was a beautiful goal,” he noted. “Everyone knows my past, I had an amazing history at Newcastle. But now I’m trying to create a new history here and I have started on the right foot.”.

What an notable week it has been for Arsenal, who have shown their squad depth by winning in Napoli then travelling to the Stadium of Light and extending their perfect start to the season to six games.

Sources indicate that other teams with aspirations of the title dropped points earlier in the day, while Arteta could battle to a win with key players brought back into the team and Guimarães coming off the bench at half-time. A trip in the Champions League followed by an away game the following weekend is a barometer of where teams are, and Arsenal have sounded a warning after coming through a bruising encounter.

According to recent reports, régis Le Bris’s team offer a challenge that is impossible to replicate, even by the standards of Arteta’s “sabotage” to make his players uncomfortable. Fans belted out Elvis Presley and 90s anthem Ready To Go just before kick-off. Then there was the aggression that Arsenal players faced. There were complaints of elbows being aimed at Gabriel Magalhães.

Bukayo Saka scored a stoppage-time penalty to seal the win but the evening belonged to Guimarães, the £75m summer signing who has been waiting for this moment to ignite his Arsenal career.

“Everyone knows I had a difficult start through injuries in my short time. But I’m glad to be back and glad to play,” Guimarães noted. “I feel very good. It was unbelievable to score a beautiful goal, beautiful moment for me and my family and I am happy.”.

According to recent reports, these are ominous signs for Arsenal’s title rivals, with Guimarães’s return to fitness adding to the midfield options. Arteta’s changes to his starting line-up restored Riccardo Calafiori and Kai Havertz – two of the in-form players in the Premier League – to the team, rather than squad players being rotated.

Sources indicate that and his players stood up to a physical challenge. Brian Brobbey used his frame to back into the Arsenal’s centre-backs, who are unlikely to given such a tough assignment this season aside from facing Erling Haaland.

Guimarães was brought on at half-time along with Jurriën Timber, which was another sign of Arsenal mounting a strong defence of their title. With Arteta’s changes altering the pace of the game, the match turned just before the hour mark. John Brooks saw nothing in the incident that floored Gabriel at a corner, but at the next set-piece penalised Ezri Konsa for wrestling with Dan Ballard, much to Arteta’s fury.

Sources indicate that le Fée had earned a point against Brentford a week earlier with a penalty, but this time his finish was tipped on to the post by David Raya. “We should not talk about the save of the keeper, we should talk about what happened before that,” added Arteta.

“But I loved the save from David, the way the team reacted, the way we go again and we go against everything, but this should never happen, it’s not fair, and I am sad, very sad, in that sense.”.

Recent findings suggest that raya also denied Nordi Mukiele from close range when Granit Xhaka’s expertly taken free-kick found his team-mate in front of goal. Sunderland have their own European campaign starting on Thursday and will start with confidence after pushing the champions all the way.

Brooks awarded a penalty in stoppage-time when Saka was brought down by Reinildo Mandava, who was dismissed. “I’m extremely pleased to win again. We had a really tough week, Chelsea, Napoli, winning there and now against a really tough opponent in a difficult place,” added Arteta.

Mikel Arteta launched a furious attack on referee John Brooks for awarding a penalty against Arsenal and fears similar decisions will cost his team the Premier League title.

Brooks gave a spot-kick for Ezri Konsa tussling with Dan Ballard, although Arteta accused the Sunderland centre-back of a “judo roll”.

Enzo Le Fée’s penalty was saved by David Raya, with Arsenal winning after goals from Bruno Guimarães and Bukayo Saka.

“In my opinion, that is not acceptable. I watched it 20 times,” stated Arteta. “And I cannot find a way to understand how you think to give a penalty in that situation or the way the VAR has to intervene.

According to recent reports, “I’m sad that we have to discuss something in such a beautiful game at this level. That has gravity because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship. And at this level, with all the work that we put in, this cannot happen.

“You see, it is a judo roll and it brings the player on the floor. So how can this happen? I cannot find an explanation. That’s why I’m trying to find that.”.

The win rounded off a positive week for Arsenal despite Arteta’s fury at the officials.

Sources indicate that “I’m extremely pleased to win again. We had a really tough week, Chelsea, Napoli, winning there and now against a really tough opponent in a difficult place. I’m very worried and very sad because this can never be a penalty ever.

In a recent development, “Are you surprised? Are you surprised? No. OK.

“I’m making it very clear publicly because it’s for the game, it’s not only for Arsenal, this cannot happen at this level. We should not talk about the save of the keeper, we should talk about what happened before that.”.

Guimarães’s goal was his first for Arsenal, with Arteta adding: “Beautiful, he came on, the goal, the assist, remarkable. That why we talk about the finishers and making that impact and being able to support and help the team. He was outstanding.”.

Three points or not, the Arsenal manager is furious about the penalty that was awarded to Sunderland.

I’m so upset – it’s unacceptable at this level. Unacceptable. This can change the course of a season, of the championship. I’ve been in football for 27 or 28 years - it’s not a penalty in any game, in any league, in any context.

Chance for Arsenal Tzolis plays a nice pass down the side of the area for Odegaard. He cuts the ball back to Havertz, who screws a first-time shot over the bar. It was a slightly awkward chance because of the angle of Odegaard’s pass.

Reinildo is booked for a foul on Saka. The home fans are getting annoyed with what they perceive as diving from some of the Arsenal attackers: “Same old Arsenal, always cheating” is the chant of choice just now. Odegaard also went down a moment ago after a foul from Angulo.

Gabriel strides forward from defence and sweeps a left-foot shot from 25 yards. It’s a good effort that fades just wide of the far post with Roefs scrambling across his line.

Sunderland will be really pleased with the first quarter. They’re defending solidly and look a threat on the break, thanks in part to some outstanding hold-up play from Brian Brobbey. Saka’s volley is the only shot on target at either end.

Chance for Sunderland Brobbey does brilliantly to hold the ball and find Le Fee, who is fouled on the left wing by Gabriel. That allows Sunderland to send the centre-backs forward - and one of them, Dan Ballard, almost opens the scoring!

In a recent development, xhaka curled a sensational ball around the Arsenal defence towards the far post, where the ball bounced up awkwardly and was knocked wide by either Ballard or Mukiele, who flew in at the far post. Ballard would have had an easier chance had Mukiele not got in the way.

According to recent reports, chance for Arsenal Saka mishits a volley straight at Roefs from close range after running onto a penetrative pass from Rice. It wasn’t an easy ball to take on the volley - Rice hit it very firmly - but Saka would usually do better.

The pattern of the game has been established, with Arsenal dominating the ball and Sunderland picking their moments to press and then counter-attack.

Sources indicate that looks like it will be a good battle between Brian Brobbey and Ezri Konsa. Brobbey seems to be attaching himself to Konsa, rather than getting into a scrap with Gabriel.

In a recent development, sunderland break promisingly down the right. Mukiele drives an angled low cross that only just evades Angulo at the far post.

Calafiori has a shot from 18 yards blocked after a typical run infield from left-back.

Industry observers note that enzo Le Fee tries to score from inside his own half. David Raya was outside the penalty area but Le Fee completely mishit the shot.

Arsenal have started well and are dominating possession. So far it’s all been in front of the Sunderland defence, but you’d expect that to change if they continue to have this much of the ball.

The champions kick off from left to right as we watch.

There’s a pulsating atmosphere at the Stadium of Light - you’d expect nothing less - and the action is about to begin.

Myles Lewis Skelly is the first England teenager to start the first four league games of a season for Arsenal since Tony Adams and David Rocastle in the 1986/87 campaign.

We’re in a congested period right now. We’re playing midweek games as well. We made four changes against Napoli, we make another four for today and we try to keep all the players connected with a high level of confidence, and with the right chemistry in and around the team.

We know how tough Sunderland made it for every opponent here [last season] and we know the beautiful atmosphere that they create, the organisation that they have and the individuals that they have. We’ll try to impose ourselves like we always do and come here and be as dominant as we’ve been and then be ready to win the game.

Arsenal’s biggest rivals are still waiting for their first win - and their first goal - of the Premier League season. Alex Connor has reaction to their 0-0 draw at home to Everton.

"For sure we can improve, and we will" 😅Mikel Arteta on Arsenal's strong start to the season 🗣️📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nDpwooZq4Y.

Arsenal keeper David Raya has conceded only one goal in five matches this season, but he was beaten twice on this ground last season during a thrilling 2-2 draw.

Sources indicate that when will Martin Zubimendi start again for Arsenal? Mikel Arteta wants to avoid a repeat of last season, when Zubimendi played more games than anyone in Europe, but it is curious that the Spaniard has not yet started a single match of this campaign. It is one thing to reduce his minutes, and another to turn him into a permanent substitute.

Recent findings suggest that zubimendi has looked quite good off the bench in recent games but has been behind Myles Lewis-Skelly and Mikel Merino in the battle to partner Declan Rice from the start. And that’s before Bruno Guimaraes, the new £75m signing, reaches full fitness.

Recent findings suggest that in the thick Naples air in midweek, Declan Rice did what he always does: he kept running. Another start for the Arsenal midfielder, another 90 minutes completed and another performance of constructive passing and destructive defending. For anyone who was worried about Rice’s physical condition, it was an emphatic response.

It has been revealed that after that Champions League victory over Napoli, Rice insisted he was ready for another marathon campaign. He made 69 appearances for club and country last season, up from 60 the previous term, and believes that is a sustainable number of games, even for an all-action midfielder such as himself. “I have shown I can do it,” he said.

According to recent reports, the key question, though, is not whether Rice can do it, but whether he should do it. There is no doubt that his body eventually began to pay the price for his exertions last year, especially during the World Cup, and it would be reasonable for his managers to worry that his extraordinary workload might one day take a serious toll. This, after all, is a footballer who managed nerve pain in his hamstring throughout the second half of last season.

Regis Le Bris, who made 11 changes for the League Cup win over Hull in midweek, reverts to the starting XI that drew at Brentford seven days ago.

Sources indicate that RLB's XI to take on Arsenal! ❤️👊#SUNARS pic.twitter.com/F1nXWky4Fp.

Mikel Arteta has made four changes to the Arsenal team that won in Napoli during the week. Kai Havertz’s return is the headline news in Arteta’s selection, with in-form left-back Riccardo Calafiori also returning. Myles Lewis-Skelly returns to the midfield and Christos Tzolis starts.

🟡 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 🔵 Your Saturday night Gunners ❤️‍🔥🤝 Presented by @deel.

Industry observers note that hello and welcome to live, minute-by-minute coverage of Sunderland v Arsenal at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland are the latest team tasked with stopping Arsenal, who have begun their title defence in formidable style: they’ve won out of three, including a dominant comeback victory against Chelsea last weekend, and look well equipped to become the first Arsenal team to retain the title since the mid-1930s.

Recent findings suggest that there’s a long way to go, and Arsenal fans will remember how blisteringly they started their last two title defences in 2002-03 and 2004-05, only to ultimately fall short. But right now, they could barely be in better shape. Their fine start to the season came with a Champions League win in Naples, achieved despite a delay to their flight from London.

“I love those challenges,” stated Mikel Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-seasons so when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.

“Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic and I don’t want the players, but not only the players, the staff as well, panicking. So when that happens, adapt to it.”.

Recent findings suggest that arteta has tested his squad in a variety of ways. “[We have] delayed the meals, delayed the transport, taken a different route. We’ve done many things – made the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less beds... because we’re going to have to adapt to different contexts.”.

So far, they’re adapting very well to the context of being the reigning champions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scegli Fcinter1908.it come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui.

In gol ancora con la Nazionale, Pio Esposito torna all’Inter dove dovrà cercare di confermarsi. Anche perché con il rientro di Lautaro e Thuram dovrà parecchio sgomitare per trovare spazio. Ne ha parlato, sulle pagine de La Gazzetta dello Sport, il giornalista Alessandro Vocalelli che fa una provocazione:.

La sosta per le nazionali ci ha consegnato tanti motivi di dibattito e regalato assolute certezze su Pio Esposito. Ce ne fosse stato bisogno, abbiamo avuto conferma delle sue qualità, della sua cifra complessiva, con la concreta speranza di aver trovato il centravanti azzurro per i prossimi 10 anni. Perché non è facile trovare un ragazzo con una personalità così spiccata e una mentalità da grande professionista: raccontano, ad esempio, che nella breve trafila tra le giovanili e i primi passi in serie B, alcuni allenatori si siano scontrati con lui per un eccesso… di impegno. Perché restava lì, un’ora in più dell’allenamento “normale”, per migliorarsi dal punto di vista atletico e tecnico. Il ritorno del campionato, come è giusto, ha però riproposto - in maniera più fragorosa - un interrogativo semplice ma efficace: ma come è possibile che il 9 dell’Italia sia poi considerato una riserva nel suo club?

In a recent development, già, perché le gerarchie sono chiare: Lautaro e Thuram sono talmente forti da meritare il ruolo di titolari e alimentare il paradosso-Esposito. Che, anche giustamente, molti tendono a dribblare con la più classica delle osservazioni: nel calcio di oggi non si gioca più in undici e avere tante soluzioni - anche a partita in corso - è solo una ricchezza. Obiezione accolta, perché questo è uno dei motivi che, in un mondo spesso divisivo, ha spinto al consenso unanime nel considerare l’Inter la più forte e più completa.

Ma, visto che parlare di calcio è un privilegio - e spesso ce ne dimentichiamo - si può provare anche ad aggiungere un po’ di sale al dibattito: per chiedersi, ad esempio, perché Lautaro, Thuram ed Esposito non potrebbero giocare insieme. La sensazione, strettamente personale, è che tre così potrebbero essere devastanti - non solo in un momento d’emergenza della gara - e in grado di compensare eventuali squilibri tattici. È chiaro, infatti, che la squadra assumerebbe un timbro ancora più spregiudicato e sarebbe necessaria una partecipazione collettiva, ma l’esperimento potrebbe riuscire in una sorta di 3-4-3 in cui esaltare le caratteristiche di partecipazione e generosità dei tre protagonisti. Perché Lautaro non è il classico centravanti d’area, ma sempre più negli anni ha dato il suo contributo in fase di costruzione e rilancio. Perché Esposito, anche lui preziosismo in area di rigore, è però un punto di riferimento potente e possente, in grado di fare da boa. E perché Thuram sa partire anche da più lontano: anzi è proprio con il campo a disposizione che risulta travolgente.

Insomma, nel pieno rispetto delle idee di Chivu e degli equilibri, forse un esperimento - o meglio un percorso - del genere potrebbe regalare ulteriore slancio ad un gruppo già fortissimo. D’altronde anche il passato e la storia insegnano molto. E - per dire quanto è strano il calcio e quanto a volte si banalizzino le discussioni - si può ad esempio ricordare il timbro che sono riusciti a dare alle loro squadre tre grandi allenatori di epoche diverse tacciati - come se fosse un’offesa - di essere “italianisti”. Eppure Trapattoni, nel 1982, giocava con Platini, Boniek, Rossi e Bettega: alla faccia di chi lo considerava un difensivista. Così Capello vinse lo scudetto alla Roma con il tridente Totti-Batistuta-Delvecchio, più due finti terzini ma in realtà ali come Cafu e Candela. E Allegri decise un giorno di lanciare una Juve con Pjanic, Cuadrado, Dybala, Higuain e Mandzukic, dando vita a una clamorosa rimonta. Ma, restando all’Inter, basta in fondo ricordare il capolavoro di Mourinho capace di conquistare il Triplete con Pandev, Milito ed Eto’o, più Sneijder alle loro spalle. A volte, insomma, basta crederci e volerlo.

Cugini sulla Lazio: “Scudetto una scommessa, ma attenzione alla stagione anomala"

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "Lo scudetto è una scommessa per la Lazio, ma l'entusiasmo dei tifosi è comprensibile".
  • In a recent development, nel corso della trasmissione Maracana, Cugini ha poi detto la sua sul tema Kean e più in generale sul Como, chiamato a gestire il doppio impegno anche con delle emergenze di organico: "Il problema di Kean non è mai stato quello del suo livello tecnico, quanto piuttosto quello del carattere.
  • According to recent reports, infine, in chiusura di blocco, si è discusso della possibilità per il Milan di acquistare Nicolò Tresoldi, attaccante italotedesco del Club Brugge.

"Lo scudetto è una scommessa per la Lazio, ma l'entusiasmo dei tifosi è comprensibile". Si potrebbe riassumere con questa frase il pensiero del giornalista della Gazzetta dello Sport Mimmo Cugini, che fra i tanti temi toccati in diretta sulla radio di Tuttomercatoweb si è soffermato sulle prospettive della squadra di Gattuso. Del resto, per completare l'intervento, Cugini ha portato a favore della sua tesi le seguenti argomentazioni: "Se facciamo una valutazione tecnica, nelle seconde scelte c'è un gap con le squadre che lottano per il titolo. Bisogna però valutare come gioca questa Lazio, perché Gattuso è riuscito a far dare ai giocatori tutto ciò che hanno e anche qualcosa in più. L'esempio più lampante è quello di Frattesi, che all'Inter era in un sistema di gioco che non lo valorizzava nonostante i gol pesanti segnati in Champions League. I giocatori della Lazio fanno quello che sanno fare e quindi ad ora viaggiano. Lo scudetto è una grande scommessa e illusione, ma capisco l'entusiasmo dei tifosi, perché una stagione in cui le altre non danno il cento per cento può capitare. Ad ora non vedo troppe squadre che possono metterla in difficoltà, ma sicuramente capiremo di più quando avrà affrontato Roma, Inter e Como. In questo momento sono sulle ali dell'entusiasmo".

In a recent development, nel corso della trasmissione Maracana, Cugini ha poi detto la sua sul tema Kean e più in generale sul Como, chiamato a gestire il doppio impegno anche con delle emergenze di organico: "Il problema di Kean non è mai stato quello del suo livello tecnico, quanto piuttosto quello del carattere. A Firenze ne ha combinate tante. Resta un giocatore di assoluto futuro, anche perché è ancora giovane. A Como il problema è quello della gestione del doppio impegno, forse anche perché non ci si aspettava di poter puntare ad andare così avanti in Champions League. C'è di conseguenza una necessità dal punto di vista numerico, perché Douvikas, per quanto bravo, non può giocare tutte le partite. I ritmi poi sono alti, anche nel nostro campionato. Non credo comunque che il Como avrà problemi ad investire viste le disponibilità economiche del club".

According to recent reports, infine, in chiusura di blocco, si è discusso della possibilità per il Milan di acquistare Nicolò Tresoldi, attaccante italotedesco del Club Brugge. A riguardo Cugini si è detto un po' scettico, incentrando le necessità dei rossoneri su altri ruoli: "Il valore del giocatore è indiscutibile, ma non vorrei che questo amore del Milan per il giocatore sia dettato dai tre gol che ha fatto all'Inter. Nell'ottica dell'attacco rossonero comunque credo che sia stato un errore tenere Camarda, che ha bisogno di giocare titolare almeno un paio d'anni da titolare in Serie B come ha fatto Pio Esposito. Detto ciò penso che i rossoneri per essere competitivi abbiano piuttosto bisogno di un grande difensore centrale e di un centrocampista, dove le alternative non sono all'altezza di Rabiot e Modric. Capisco che il nome entusiasmi il tifoso, ma intanto bisogna vedere se il Brugge sia disposto a cederlo, dato che è pur sempre una bottega cara. Credo che almeno al 60% questa operazione alla fine non si farà".
